news.Title: The 1 Thing I'd Want Elon Musk to Answer on Tesla's Oct. 21 Call
news.Content:
Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) will release its third-quarter results after the close on Wednesday, Oct. 21, with a live webcast to follow at 5:30 p.m. Eastern time. Some of the quarter is already known. The EV maker said it delivered 486,532 vehicles in the period, up about 1% from the second quarter.

Shares trade around $367 as of this writing, about 25% under their record close of $489.88 in December 2025.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Most of the attention on the call will likely turn to Tesla's profit margins. But I'd say the answer that matters most for the stock won't be in the earnings report at all. If I could ask CEO Elon Musk one thing, it'd be this: How much does Tesla earn per paid Robotaxi mile after the cost of running the car?

Image source: Getty Images.

Earnings alone can't carry this stock

Tesla is selling more but keeping less. Second-quarter revenue grew 26% year over year, yet its non-GAAP (adjusted) earnings per share dropped 18% to $0.33. Just 1.4% of revenue was left as operating profit.

Now imagine the third quarter comes in much better than that. If adjusted earnings per share doubled to $0.66 and Tesla kept that pace for a full year, the stock would still trade at around 140 times earnings. Using expected 2027 earnings, the price-to-earnings ratio is about 165.

Put simply, I don't think even a great quarter can come close to explaining a stock priced like this.

"[O]ver time, we expect our hardware-related profits to be accompanied by an acceleration of AI, software and fleet-based profits," Tesla said in its second-quarter update.

The largest source of those fleet-based profits will likely be Robotaxi, Tesla's driverless ride-hailing service. It's arguably where most of the stock's value sits now.

What does a Robotaxi mile earn?

Tesla hasn't said.

The company offers lots of other Robotaxi details. Its second-quarter update graphed cumulative paid Robotaxi miles and named seven major metro areas where the service runs -- six of them with no safety driver at the wheel. And on Sept. 3, Tesla's vice president of AI, Ashok Elluswamy, said Robotaxi had topped 1 million unsupervised miles, up from the more than 380,000 he cited on the July earnings call.

Also, Tesla has started making the Cybercab, its steering-wheel-free car for the fleet, at its Texas plant, where it lists installed capacity of over 125,000 Cybercabs a year. Tesla began offering Cybercab rides to the public in Austin in early September.

Story Continues

But Tesla doesn't share what Robotaxi takes in or what it costs to run. And these costs could be significant. In its last quarterly filing, Tesla said it's building infrastructure for the service, such as vehicle cleaning and maintenance, charging, security, teleoperations (remote support), and fleet management.

Musk, of course, is confident. On the second-quarter call, he said "the economics will be so compelling" that he expects demand for Robotaxi to outpace Tesla's ability to meet it.

That might prove right. But for now, investors are paying for those economics without a per-mile number to check them against.

Tesla's spending is rising fast

Tesla is also spending a lot as investors wait. Capital expenditures were around $5.8 billion in the second quarter, up 142% from a year before, and management expects over $25 billion for 2026. That spending drove free cash flow to negative $1.1 billion that quarter, down from positive $146 million a year before. And chief financial officer Vaibhav Taneja said capital spending "will grow for the next two to three years" as Tesla expands its Robotaxi fleet, among other projects.

Musk said he's confident the investments will bring "really the best CapEx returns that we've ever seen." Robotaxi's per-mile economics would be one of the first ways for investors to check that claim.

Yes, Robotaxi is still in its early days, and one number can't settle a bet this big. Costs per mile could also drop as the fleet grows. But it would show whether Robotaxi already makes money on every ride, or how far it still has to go.

In the end, if Musk shares a per-mile profit that holds up after charging, cleaning, remote support, and wear on the cars, I'd take a much closer look at the stock. It would help even more if Tesla started reporting Robotaxi results separately. But if he gives just another forecast, I think shares still look too pricey at around 165 times expected 2027 earnings.

news.Title: Can Apple Overtake Nvidia as the World's Largest Company in 2027?
news.Content:
Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) has closed the gap with first-place Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) as the world's largest company. Apple is about ready to cross the $5 trillion valuation threshold, while Nvidia has faltered a bit in recent days and is valued at just under $5.5 trillion. But can Apple overtake Nvidia over the next year?

As long as the artificial intelligence build-out progresses as every company has guided for, I'd say the answer is a resounding "No." Nvidia's growth will be too much for Apple to compete with, resulting in Nvidia opening a commanding lead that may never be closed.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Why has Apple been succeeding recently?

On paper, Apple isn't the most impressive company. In its most recent quarter, it grew revenue by 16%. That's not bad, but it doesn't hold a candle to the 106% growth Nvidia delivered during its last quarterly earnings report. But I don't think that's the point.

Apple hasn't gone all-in on AI like some of its peers have. In fact, its capital expenditures have fallen in recent quarters.

AAPL Capital Expenditures (TTM) data by YCharts

Over the past 12 months, Apple's capital expenditures have totaled a mere $10 billion. If you look at some of the big AI hyperscalers, they're spending up to and over $200 billion this year alone. That makes many investors nervous, so they're shifting into a company that isn't going all-in, yet still has some tech exposure. As a result, Apple has become a popular stock pick for those wanting to escape the AI investment trend. However, this excitement has led to Apple's valuation swelling.

From a price-to-earnings (P/E) standpoint, Nvidia's value is far lower than Apple's.

This is odd for a handful of reasons, but first and foremost is growth. If you were handed two stocks in a blindfolded test where one is growing at a 16% rate and valued at 39 times earnings, and another is growing at a 106% rate and valued at 29 times earnings, you'd pick the higher growth, lower valued stock every time. But because it has "AI" attached to it, the market isn't in love with Nvidia's stock like it is with Apple's.

I think this is a major mistake, and this mistake is your opportunity to make a boatload of money.

None of Nvidia's projected 2027 growth is priced into the stock

Nvidia's 29-times-earnings valuation is pretty average for where most big tech stocks have historically traded. However, Nvidia is expected to produce extraordinary growth in 2027. In its most recent conference call, Nvidia informed investors that it expects 70% revenue growth next year. Clearly, there's plenty of AI growth left in the tank for Nvidia, and this will result in Nvidia opening up its lead.

Story Continues

As of now, almost none of Nvidia's 2027 growth is priced into the stock, as it trades for a mere 14 times next year's earnings.

AAPL PE Ratio (Forward 1y) data by YCharts

Meanwhile, Apple trades at 31 times earnings. If Nvidia's results come in as expected and the stock can rise to its current 29 times trailing earnings by the end of next fiscal year, it would indicate that Nvidia will double. That would open up a huge gap between it and Apple, and all it has to do is return to a pretty reasonable price tag and execute.

That's a low bar to clear, and I think it makes it pretty clear that Nvidia will still be a larger company than Apple next year, as long as the AI build-out progresses as everyone expects.

news.Title: TSMC Open to Working With Terafab But Must Control Plants
news.Content:
(Bloomberg) -- Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. is in discussions about collaborating with Elon Musk's Terafab project, though the Asian chipmaker stressed it must control its chip production in any alliance.

Most Read from Bloomberg

CoreWeave's Big Dream Crashes Into Reality as Yields Top 15%

Stocks Fall on Inflation Woes as Chip Rout Deepens: Markets Wrap

China's Backdoor Bond-Buying Talk Swirls on $600 Billion Buildup

CoreWeave's Bonds Turn Distressed, Drawing 'Yikes' From Musk

Apple Unveils $299 HomeView Hub as Part of New Smart Home Push

Asked if TSMC was joining Musk's ambitious endeavor to get into chipmaking, Chief Executive Officer C. C. Wei said his company must operate its fabrication plants. Those comments followed the billionaire entrepreneur's assertion last week that Taiwan's largest company would at most only lease capacity rather than run manufacturing.

"We are still in discussion, let me say that," Wei told analysts on a conference call. "But the fab has got to be run by TSMC."

Based in Texas, the Terafab project is Musk's effort to break into the business of fabricating chips, in service of his companies Tesla Inc. and SpaceXAI. Responding to speculation about TSMC potentially coming in to run operations, the Tesla chief said that his companies would be solely in charge at Terafab. Neither side has specified the parameters of any arrangement under discussion beyond confirming the talks.

US chipmaker Intel Corp. is helping Musk's companies with developing the technology that'll go inside the Terafab. The facility is expected to supply advanced semiconductors for the needs of Musk's empire, across the Tesla carmaking and robotics business and the consolidated SpaceXAI that includes both spacefaring technology and the xAI group developing Grok. Musk has stressed that his companies would "build and run the fab."

news.Title: Google Just Started Paying SpaceX $920 Million a Month. Here's What That's Worth per Share.
news.Content:
This month marks the first payment of a major compute-rental contract for Space Exploration Technologies (NASDAQ: SPCX). Alphabet 's Google agreed to pay the space company $920 million a month for access to about 110,000 Nvidia GPUs in a deal that runs from October 2026 through June 2029.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

SpaceX has about 13.2 billion shares outstanding, so some quick math shows how much this compute deal is worth per share.

At the contract's monthly rate, Google will pay SpaceX about $11 billion a year and about $30 billion over the full 33-month term. That comes out to approximately $0.07 in sales per share per month, $0.83 in sales per share per year, and $2.27 in sales per share over the entire term.

SpaceX has a market cap of $2.2 trillion as of Oct. 12, so $11 billion in annual sales is a small amount by comparison. It's more significant when compared with SpaceX's revenue. The space company reported revenue of $20.7 billion over the trailing 12 months. This contract alone could increase yearly revenue by over 50%, and SpaceX has secured an even more lucrative deal with Anthropic for up to $84.5 billion through May 2029.

The catch is that SpaceX's deals with Google and Anthropic include 90-day mutual cancellation clauses, giving each side the option to walk away with 90 days' notice after an initial period. Investors shouldn't look at SpaceX's compute-rental contracts as guaranteed long-term income. Still, these agreements are promising signs that the company's AI segment will become a profitable part of its business and help justify the premium valuation on SpaceX stock .

news.Title: TSMC Q3 profit surges to record high on AI demand; says considering Texas fab
news.Content:
Investing.com-- Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co, or TSMC, clocked a stronger-than-expected third-quarter profit on Thursday, with earnings hitting another record high on robust demand from the artificial intelligence industry.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

The company said that it had considered setting up more facilities in the U.S., potentially in Texas, as it races to ramp up capacity and meet increasing demand.

The world's largest contract chipmaker said net profit surged to T$763.06 billion ($23.55 billion) in the three months to September 30. The print jumped nearly 69% year-on-year to a record high, and was also well above Reuters/LSEG estimates of T$746.3 billion.

Revenue jumped 50% to T$1.49 trillion. Gross margin was 66.4%, operating margin was 58.7%, and net profit margin was 51.1%, TSMC said.

Capacity buildout to dent margins, TSMC looking at Texas fab

Speaking in a post-earnings webcast, CFO Wendell Huang warned of a continued deterioration in TSMC's gross margins from the company's attempts to increase capacity-- both at home and abroad-- to meet growing chip demand.

Gross margin dilution from the buildout is expected to be closer to 2% in 2026, Huang said, while margin dilution from its overseas facilities was expected to be higher in the coming years. He forecast an at least 0.4% drop in fourth-quarter gross margin.

He said that capital spending was expected to be "significantly higher" in the coming years, citing continued, outsized demand from AI, which required more production capacity.

Huang reiterated TSMC's 2026 capital budget of between $60 billion and $65 billion. He declined to provide a number on just how much capacity will increase in the coming months.

"We're working very hard to increase our capacity in the U.S.," CEO C.C. Wei said in response to an analyst question. Wei said the company had looked at U.S.-based locations outside its primary Arizona site in the U.S., including in Texas, for more facilities.

Wei said the company was still in discussions over the nature of the facilities, on whether they will be run directly by TSMC or as part of a tie-up with partners such as Elon Musk's Terrafab.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

AI-driven demand to remain very strong

Huang said TSMC revenue will be between $52.3 billion and $54.3 billion, representing a 58% year-on-year increase.

Story Continues

Separately, CEO C.C. Wei forecast 2026 revenue growth to be around 44% year-on-year in USD terms.

"The AI market continues to be very strong... we observe increasing AI demand, fueled by the increasing adoption of agentic AI," Wei said.

"The value of semiconductors in the global AI chain is expected to continue to increase."

Thursday's print marked a sixth straight quarter of record profits for TSMC, and an 11th straight quarter of growth, as the chipmaker continued to reap great returns from AI-fueled demand.

The company's advanced 2-nanometer chips accounted for 8% of total wafer revenue, while 3-nm accounted for 33% of revenue.

The company is the world's largest contract chipmaker by production capacity, and also manufactures the most advanced chips in the market. This position saw TSMC benefit greatly from increasing global demand for advanced AI processors, with NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ:NVDA) being among its biggest customers.

The company is also widely regarded as a bellwether for global chip demand.

TSMC's earnings were preceded by a strong showing from chipmaking equipment major ASML Holding NV (AS:ASML), which also flagged strong AI-fueled demand earlier this week.

Still, TSMC's earnings come amid a deep rout in chipmaking and AI equity valuations, as the prospect of rising U.S. interest rates battered the debt-heavy sector.

news.Title: 台股收盤／台股寫史上第6大跌點！崩1655點櫃買跌5.53%　這些族群倒地
news.Content:
美國通膨高於預期引爆賣壓，台股今（15）日收盤暴跌1655.96點，收46,969.87點，創下史上第6大跌點，櫃買指數重挫5.53%，兩市場成交金額合計突破1.56兆元，台積電下跌50元，市場一片慘綠。

美通膨超出預期引爆恐慌　台股暴跌創史上第6大跌點

美國最新公布9月消費者物價指數（CPI）年增率由8月的3.4%攀升至3.7%，高於市場預期，月增率由0.4%加速至0.6%，符合預期；核心CPI年增2.6%、月增0.3%，雙雙高於預期。加上市場擔憂人工智慧（AI）業者過度仰賴舉債支應龐大建設支出，拖累美股四大指數同步收黑，科技股賣壓尤其沉重，也讓台股面臨沉重壓力。

台股今日開盤即遭遇猛烈賣壓，盤中雖一度反彈，但買盤無力扭轉跌勢，終場加權指數收在46,969.87點，下跌1655.96點，跌幅3.41%，失守4萬7千點整數關卡，創下史上第6大跌點，上市成交金額高達1兆3197.7億元，呈現價跌量增格局。

代表中小型股的櫃買指數跌勢更加慘烈，終場收396.90點，下跌23.23點，跌幅達5.53%，成交金額2439.03億元，上市櫃合計成交金額高達1兆5636.73億元，顯示市場交易極為熱絡，但資金主要集中在震盪與賣壓之中。

從市場漲跌家數觀察，上市股票下跌達1016家，上漲僅250家；上櫃股票下跌882家，上漲230家，上市櫃合計下跌家數達1898家，反映這波跌勢不僅集中大型權值股，中小型股票同樣受到衝擊。

倫元投顧陳學進分析師認為，受到美國9月通膨高於預期，市場押注Fed本月再升息的機率攀升，以及市場擔憂人工智慧(AI)業者過度仰賴舉債支應龐大建設支出的夾擊，導致相關AI晶片股及科技股籠罩在一股惶恐與不安的漩窩之中，加上融資餘額居高不下，因此，隨著高檔獲利了結賣壓與融資清洗賣壓正在同步釋放的衝擊下，於是引發今日出現「多殺多」的格局，不論是ASIC設計、PCB/CCL、CPO光通訊、高速傳輸連接器、玻纖布、記憶體、被動元件、矽晶圓、先進封裝與設備、或是台塑四寶…等均無法倖免於難、甚至許多股票紛紛遭受到無情砍殺摜壓至跌停板；在下檔在季線震盪向上不變、具有強力支撐下，今日殺過頭之後，預期明日見低之後，將隨時可望觸底反彈上漲上來；面對利空衝擊恐慌下殺的過程中，此時最重要的是：對於某些高估值之漲高股，以及產業前景不如預期的公司，宜速速避開之，萬不可貿然搶進，宜採取「反彈汰弱留強、拉回低接優質股」的策略外；但是，對於某些具有實質基本面支撐、流動性佳的AI受惠股、且產業趨勢明確、低基期的族群，若此時能夠展現相對抗跌的韌性，則逢低仍可留意。

台積電跌50元拖累大盤　聯發科、台達電、南亞科全面倒地

news.Title: 台股炸出1.32兆元巨量！分析師：恐慌大打折 官股、法人、散戶全衝了
news.Content:
台股今（15）日收盤重挫1,655點，創下史上第六大跌點，全日更爆出1.32兆元的歷史級巨量。對此，兩位受訪分析師指出，八大官股、投信法人與內資散戶已紛紛進場抄底撿便宜，一位分析師更直呼「恐慌情緒大打折，不該進場嗎？」

台股15日開低走低，盤中一度重挫1,830點，終場大跌1,655.96點（跌幅3.41%），收在46,970點，創下台股史上第六大收盤跌點。 全日成交量爆出 1.3197兆元（約1.32兆元） 巨量，顯示多空交戰極為激烈，倫元投顧分析師王春盛表示，八大官股、投信法人及內資散戶進場抄底撿便宜。

倫元投顧分析師王春盛表示，今日大盤盤中重挫1,830點後跌幅逐漸收斂，成交量衝上1.32兆元，充分展現多空雙方激烈交戰。雖然市場寄望官股、投信與散戶進場能帶動低接買盤，但必須強調「爆量並不代表底部已經確立」。

王春盛指出，後續盤勢能否止穩，關鍵在於兩大指標：一是權值股能否率先止跌，二是尾盤能否持續收斂跌幅。

在操作建議上，現階段不宜急著重押搶反彈，建議投資人優先選擇基本面佳、業績有支撐的個股，採取分批布局並保留充足現金，同時嚴守停損。若未來幾天呈現「量增且指數持續收復失土」，才有利於短線止穩；反之若再度放量下殺，仍須嚴防賣壓延續。

資深台股分析師蔡明翰：市場恐慌過頭 逢大打折可布局

資深台股分析師蔡明翰則從市場情緒切入分析，指出今日大盤暴跌的主因在於「市場情緒極度恐慌與不理性」。

蔡明翰認為，面對這種非理性的恐慌拋售潮，往往就是優質標的獲得大打折的時刻。「今天大打折你不買，什麼時候買？」他直言，對於中長期投資人而言，當市場陷入極度恐慌時，反而不需要過度悲觀，「進場就對了」，可趁大盤大幅拉回時尋找被錯殺的優質標的擇優布局。

陳依旻／財經特派記者副組長，主跑央行、證交所、投信投顧等

news.Title: 台積電第三季EPS衝上29.43元創新高 2奈米佔比首達8％
news.Content:
晶圓代工龍頭台積電15日公布第3季財報，受惠市場對高效能運算及智慧型手機晶片需求暢旺，單季合併營收達1兆4942億4千萬元，稅後純益衝上7630億6千萬元，每股盈餘（EPS）繳出29.43元的歷史新高成績，較去年同期大幅增長68.7％。

台積電第3季美元營收為467.2億元，年增41.2％、季增16.2％。在獲利能力指標方面，第3季毛利率繳出66.4％高水準，營業利益率達58.7％，稅後純益率則為51.1％。相較前一季，單季毛利來到9,923億7,900萬元，季增15.4％；營業利益為8,764億4,500萬元，季增14.3％；稅前純益更達到9,110億3,900萬元，年增73.4％。

在各先進製程銷售比重部分，最新量產的2奈米製程在第3季首度貢獻業績，佔全季晶圓銷售金額的8％；3奈米製程為營收主力，佔比達33％；5奈米製程佔28％；7奈米製程則佔10％。總計包含7奈米及更先進製程在內的先進製程營收，已佔全季晶圓銷售總額的79％。

總結第3季財務表現，台積電單季營收與稅後純益同步改寫歷史新猷，單季獲利正式突破7,600億元關卡。在3奈米與5奈米持續貢獻主要營收動能之際，2奈米製程亦順利跨入量產放量階段，整體先進製程比重逼近8成，推動各項獲利數據繳出全面成長的營運成績。

news.Title: 史上第六慘！台股收盤慘跌1655點 後市看他表現
news.Content:
台股今（15日）盤中一度下殺1830.45點觸及46795.38點，跌幅達3.8%，尾盤跌勢略微收斂，終場下跌1655.96點收在46969.87點，改寫史上第六大跌點。半導體與電子股成為重災區，台積電下跌50元收在2440元，聯發科跌310元收在4165元，台達電重挫155元收在1630元，鴻海也跌逾1%，日月光、緯穎跌停，台光電也重挫7.25%。

金融股與內需族群苦撐，熱門族群光通訊、PCB、光學、記憶體、航運及漲多的傳產都下挫，觀察類股指數，僅食品、造紙、觀光餐旅、汽車、百貨貿易、運動休閒及居家生活收紅，上市櫃超過千家下殺。

台股今改寫史上第六慘跌點，最大跌點是今年7月17日寫下的2953.71點，第二大跌點則是去年4月關稅戰的2065.87點，第三大跌點今年7月28日的重挫2030.83點，第四大是2024年8月5日的下跌1807.21點，第五大是今年6月26日暴跌1683.59點。

美國消費者物價指數超過預期，使美股持續回檔，費城半導體族群成為箭靶，半導體與人工智慧族群佔比高的台日韓股也跟著下殺，日股慘崩超過3%，韓股更是一口氣暴跌逾7%，險些熔斷，已接近7月股災時的低點。

升息機率升高，加上人工智慧隱憂仍在，鉅額借貸面臨無法兌現鉅額投資的考驗，多重利空衝擊使漲多的族群無一倖免。展望後市，法人認為，台股想要止穩必須觀察國際股市動向，並留意台積電法說會的財測與表現。

news.Title: TSMC’s Profit Surpasses Expectations After AI Orders Rush In
news.Content:
(Bloomberg) -- Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. reported a better-than-expected profit for the September quarter, sustaining torrid growth despite rising concern about the long-term AI buildout.

Most Read from Bloomberg

CoreWeave's Big Dream Crashes Into Reality as Yields Top 15%

Stocks Fall on Inflation Woes as Chip Rout Deepens: Markets Wrap

CoreWeave's Bonds Turn Distressed, Drawing 'Yikes' From Musk

Apple Unveils $299 HomeView Hub as Part of New Smart Home Push

Epic Games Delays Disney Project, Asks Developers to Use More AI

The global chipmaking linchpin said net income rose 69% to NT$763.1 billion ($23.6 billion), more than the average analyst estimate. That came after the company reported a sales jump of 51% in the period, also above expectations, taking its revenue across the three months to $47 billion.

The exclusive chipmaker of Nvidia Corp. and Apple Inc.'s most advanced semiconductors, TSMC offered a counterpoint to increasingly negative sentiment around AI-linked names. Downstream from the chipmaker, worries about return on investments and long-term financing are hurting companies like cloud provider and Nvidia customer CoreWeave Inc., which on Wednesday saw its stock and bond prices plunge in a widespread selloff.

Click here for a liveblog of the results.

TSMC, for its part, has seen sales growth accelerate over the past two quarters and has ramped up capacity expansion. The company has said its capital expenditures will reach as much as $64 billion, a record, this year.

Hsinchu-based TSMC serves as a key barometer of global AI demand as every major industry player including Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices Inc. and Alphabet Inc.'s Google rely on the Taiwanese chipmaker to turn their most cutting-edge designs into physical components.

TSMC's shares touched a record this month, among the first chip stocks globally to set a new high after a July market rout. It's been outperforming peers thanks to a dominant position in the manufacturing of processors needed to power AI. Yet it got caught up in the broader pullback in tech stocks over the past week.

Read: TSMC Results Face High Bar to Calm Global AI Stock Trade Jitters

Consensus estimates have been climbing for the Taiwanese firm's 2027 capital spending, a key indicator for the industry. Goldman Sachs Group Inc. now targets $85 billion and UBS Group AG $90 billion, compared with the $75 billion average of firms polled by Bloomberg.

The company is now trying to build and furnish about 20 factories at home and overseas, an unprecedented pace for a company that typically works on four or five new buildings simultaneously.

Story Continues

On top of its $265 billion pledge to build a campus in Arizona, the company is now considering an additional US site in Texas due to the rush in the US to build data centers, Bloomberg News has reported.

What Bloomberg Intelligence Says

The bigger 3Q questions are about 2027. TSMC's Arizona expansion, a possible Texas hub and Terafab talks could shape capex and overseas margin dilution, while Taiwan reports point to 3-6% wafer-price increases. Updates on the next-generation A14 processing node and advanced packaging should also clarify TSMC's response to Intel's challenge.

- Charles Shum, analyst

news.Title: 【台積電法說會】第三季每股賺破29元！年增近7成 毛利率下滑
news.Content:
台積電今（15）日舉辦第三季法說會，第三季合併營收約新台幣1兆4,942億4千萬元，稅後純益約新台幣7,630億6千萬元，每股盈餘為新台幣29.43元，和去年同期的17.44元相比，年增近七成，但毛利率微幅下滑，從68％變成66%。

與去年同期相較，2026年第三季營收增加了50.9%，稅後純益與每股盈餘皆增加了68.7%。與前一季相較，2026年第三季營收增加了17.6%，稅後純益則增加了8.0%。以上財務數字皆為合併財務報表數字，且係依照金管會認可之國際財務報導準則（TIFRS）所編製。

若以美元計算，2026年第三季營收為467.2億，較去年同期增加了41.2%，較前一季增加了16.2%。

2026年第三季毛利率為66.4%，營業利益率為58.7%，稅後純益率則為51.1%。

2奈米製程出貨佔台積公司2026年第三季晶圓銷售金額的8%；3奈米製程出貨佔全季晶圓銷售金額的33%，5奈米製程出貨佔全季晶圓銷售金額的28%；7奈米製程出貨則佔全季晶圓銷售金額的10%。總體而言，先進製程（包含7奈米及更先進製程）的營收達到全季晶圓銷售金額的79%。

news.Title: 字節跳動傳擬洽購聯發科AI晶片 用於資料中心
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-10-15 13:26:39 新聞中心 發佈

綜合陸媒及港媒報導，據外媒引述消息人士指出，字節跳動即將達成協議，採購用於資料中心的聯發科(2454)客製化AI晶片。這筆交易既能為字節跳動拿到關鍵算力元器件，也能幫助聯發科與高通展開競爭。知情人士透露，字節跳動正與聯發科深入洽談供應客製化晶片事宜，這些晶片將用於字節跳動的資料中心。聯發科將提供數量待定的專用積體電路(ASIC)，即根據客戶平台需求定制的晶片。如果交易達成，字節跳動或將成為聯發科ASIC業務繼Alphabet旗下Google之後的第二大客戶。

據悉，字節跳動正在加大硬體支出，押注AI成為其下一個增長引擎。但與阿里巴巴(9988.HK)和騰訊(0700.HK)等中國競爭對手一樣，字節跳動無法採購輝達(NVIDIA)等廠商最頂尖的AI晶片；而華為等本土晶片廠商也難以完全滿足其全部算力需求。因此字節跳動正尋找替代方案，包括和晶片設計公司合作。在目前美國出口管制規則下，只要中國企業採購的AI算力不超過特定閾值，這類合作模式是允許的。外媒先前報導，字節跳動今年即已與高通達成類似協議，採購數百萬顆AI晶片。

此外，字節跳動考慮將今年資本開支最高提升至700億美元，是去年總額兩倍以上，用於擴建資料中心與其他AI基礎設施。如果經濟與經營環境趨好，2027年資本開支或將進一步達到1,000億美元。此外，字節跳動在9月獲得了一筆300億美元貸款，為相關投入提供資金。字節跳動的大手筆投入，代表其正採取更為激進的策略，希望在對話大模型、影片生成等關鍵領域鞏固先發優勢，並擴大海外影響力，而公司AI業務以Seedance等旗艦模型為核心，面臨來自阿里Happy Horse、快手(1024.HK)可靈AI以及Google等強勁對手的競爭。

news.Title: 台股雪崩式急殺逾千點 台積電與三星等大廠組「復仇者聯盟」
news.Content:
受到週三（14日）美股四大主要指數全面走跌的打擊，今（15）日台股開盤就面臨龐大賣壓，早盤指數雪崩式走低，一度下跌破千點，並持續下探；其中，晶圓代工龍頭台積電，今日下午要召開第三季法說會，儘管外資給予高預期，反觀股價卻沒有出現押寶行情。但除了股價表現，國際上更關注台積電正在跟三星、英特爾等大廠合作，籌組全球晶片聯盟要對抗快速崛起的中國勢力。

法說會押寶行情落空 台積電盤中一度跌70元

盤面一片綠油油，週四台股開盤面臨龐大賣壓，加權指數雪崩式走低，早盤一度崩跌超過1400點，除了電子零組件、AI概念股殺聲隆隆，就連台積電15日下午要召開第三季法說會，股價也沒出現押寶卡位行情，跌勢同樣驚人。

永豐期貨分析師劉佳倫指出，「（美國）偏中小型的這種雲端廠商，因為他們的一個債信有點狀況，然後市場上會怕怕的，要能夠讓台積電變成全村的希望，除了開出來的財報好於預期之外，未來它對資本支出也好，或者是它未來的一個相關的訂單的展望（也要好）。」

抗中國勢力 台積電、三星、英特爾組「全球晶片聯盟」

面對波動加劇，有分析師直呼，目前先觀望就好。但除了關注台股短線震盪，全球半導體產業的競爭也正進入新一輪布局。

韓國媒體報導，台積電正在和三星、SK海力士、英特爾等大廠合作，籌組「全球晶片聯盟」，總投資額高達50億美元，這是全球最大的半導體製程技術及製造設備，一同聯合研發設施，希望透過這個全球性聯盟，加快半導體創新，而背後原因和中國記憶體廠快速崛起有關。

台積電與大廠合作，籌組全球晶片聯盟。圖／台視新聞製作

劉佳倫表示，「比較像是在因應說未來長期，他們要繼續保有他們的一個技術的護城河，當然還是會有人擔心會不會說表面上合作，但私下又在競爭，技術上可以合作，但是訂單上應該還是屬於一個比較偏良性競爭。」

只是一方面是合作夥伴，一方面台積電也和英特爾與三星進入三強競逐，而台積電法說會能否替市場注入信心，也將牽動大盤接下來的走勢。

台北／魏于恬　編輯／賀澤佳

news.Title: 獲美日210億美元建廠計畫挹注，格羅方德週三漲4.8%、費半唯一收紅個股
news.Content:
【財訊快報／陳孟朔】格羅方德(GlobalFoundries，美股代碼GFS)傳將在日本政府最高210億美元資金支持下，於美國紐約州北部新建兩座晶片廠，成為半導體股全面下挫中的亮點。該股週三(14日)收盤上漲2.24美元或4.80%，報48.94美元，成為費城半導體指數成分股中碩果僅存的唯一收紅個股，與費半當日重挫4.30%形成強烈對比。根據週三宣布的協議，新廠將由美國與日本共同擁有，交由格羅方德營運，資金來自日本承諾的5,500億美元對美投資計畫，協議並包括美國持有格羅方德4%股權。這項安排結合日本資金、美國在地製造及格羅方德營運能力，凸顯美日正透過跨國投資合作，擴充美國半導體生產基礎。

消息激勵格羅方德週三盤中一度上漲6.60%，收盤保住大部分漲幅；截至週二，該股今年已累計上漲約34%。在AI融資疑慮、利率預期與高估值壓力拖累晶片股之際，具體建廠資金及政策支持提供個股支撐，也使其走勢明顯優於同業。

後續市場將關注資金撥付條件、兩座新廠的建設時程、製程與客戶布局，以及美國取得4%股權的具體安排。最高210億美元支持規模並不等同格羅方德可立即認列的營收或獲利，新廠對營運的實際貢獻，仍取決於建設進度、量產效率與訂單需求。

news.Title: Mamdani's $29M quantum deal sparks panic: 'Is Zohran coming for our coins..'
news.Content:
Google has warned that future quantum computers could let thieves steal cryptocurrency by breaking the security used to approve payments.

New York is now investing $29.2 million in an NYU lab where researchers will make and test quantum chips and components.

To understand why the deal drew alarm from Bitcoin investor Nic Carter, start with how someone proves that they can spend their coins.

How a quantum attack could steal Bitcoin

A Bitcoin private key is a secret number that lets its holder authorize payments. Wallet software uses that number to produce a digital signature, which the Bitcoin network checks before accepting a payment.

A public key is a related number that allows the network to check the signature without revealing the private key. Knowing the public key should not let anyone else spend the coins.

A powerful enough quantum computer could break that protection by calculating the private key from the public key, according to Bitcoin Optech . A thief with that private key could then sign a payment sending the victim's coins to the thief.

The coins at risk in this type of attack are those whose public keys an attacker can see. Google recommends avoiding the exposure or reuse of vulnerable wallet addresses while the cryptocurrency industry works on stronger protection.

Related: Quantum threat forces 63-year old investment bank to abandon Bitcoin

This is not a claim that today's quantum computers can empty Bitcoin wallets. The attack requires a machine powerful and reliable enough to finish the calculation, and Google's research does not announce such a machine.

The reason to prepare now is that Google's March 31 study lowered its estimate of the resources a future attacker would need.

Under specified hardware assumptions, researchers estimated that a machine with fewer than 500,000 quantum bits, or qubits, could complete the calculation in minutes.

That estimate is a warning to improve security before the machine exists, not evidence that Bitcoin has already been broken. It explains why new investment in quantum research attracts attention from Bitcoin holders, even when the research has other stated goals.

What the city is building

Mamdani's Oct. 14 announcement commits $29.2 million to QFab, a quantum fabrication facility at NYU. The university is contributing another $255 million for construction and 10 years of operations.

Expected to open in 2030, the 23,000-square-foot facility at 770 Broadway will provide equipment for making and testing quantum chips and components.

Story Continues

Think of QFab as a place to develop the pieces, not an announcement that a code-breaking machine is ready. Its cleanrooms, testing equipment and cryogenic systems will be available to researchers, students, startups and established companies, according to the city's release .

That work could help advance quantum technology, which is why Bitcoin holders have a reason to watch it. But neither the city nor NYU's announcement identifies cryptocurrency attacks as a purpose, and neither presents a demonstration of one.

Mamdani described a different ambition: technologies that could change how people fight disease, store energy and exchange information.

"We want those technologies, investments and jobs to be created here in New York City," the mayor said in the public announcement. The city also promises training opportunities for CUNY and public-school students, linking the research investment to a local workforce.

Popular on TheStreet Roundtable:

Morgan Stanley's new lab to test Wall Street's future

IMF ranks Ondo among largest tokenized asset issuers

JPMorgan says one asset class could soon beat gold

Why Carter's reaction fits the bigger fear

Carter, a founding partner of Castle Island Ventures and a cofounder of crypto-data company Coin Metrics , responded to coverage of the deal with a blunt question.

"Is zohran is coming for our coins," he wrote.

The remark connects the mayor's investment to an existing Bitcoin anxiety, it does not establish that Mamdani plans to seize cryptocurrency. The project's publicly stated goals remain research, training and commercial development.

What New Yorkers get in return

The city's answer is a voice in QFab and a share of certain future proceeds. New York will receive three seats on the facility's Executive Advisory Board.

The financial agreement is more specific than a claim that taxpayers get 15% of everything the lab produces.

When intellectual property is created using city-funded tools, New York will receive 15% of NYU Central Administration's proceeds from that intellectual property, according to the announcement. Those proceeds can include equity, royalties, milestone payments and patent licenses.

That is not a 15% stake in every company using QFab, and it is not a guaranteed return. The value depends on what gets invented, what succeeds commercially and what proceeds reach the university administration.

Deputy Mayor for Economic Justice Julie Su put the principle simply:

"When the public invests in a new technology at the start, the public should share in the success."

The problem Bitcoin has to solve

Quantum-resistant alternatives are known, but adopting them would mean changes to Bitcoin's security design, with trade-offs such as larger signatures, Bitcoin Optech explains .

Research into those changes is not the same as a completed network upgrade.

Google is urging the cryptocurrency industry to prepare, not declaring that the system has already failed.

Its separate 2029 target is a deadline for moving its own systems toward post-quantum cryptography, not a prediction that Bitcoin will be broken that year. QFab's expected 2030 opening is likewise a construction timetable, not a date for a cryptocurrency attack.

news.Title: 台股慘崩1800點！抄底族狂搶不只爆買友達  第1名竟是這檔
news.Content:
受美國通膨升息疑慮及晶片股拋售潮衝擊，日韓股市周四（15日）大幅狂瀉，台股盤中也面臨劇烈賣壓，一度暴跌超過1800點，失守47000點大關，最低下探至46795點。儘管大盤重挫，市場抄底買盤踴躍，成交量前10名中由ETF佔據9檔，包括友達、有瑤池金母封號的00981A都入列，反映散戶與法人資金逢低布局意願強烈。

截至12時26分左右，加權指數達46957點，跌1668點（或3.4%），成交金額1.06兆元。

據最新成交量統計，市場資金高度集中於ETF標的。成交量冠軍由「主動中信台灣收益」（00406A）以135.3萬張奪下，成交金額達127.75億元；「群益臺灣加權正2」（00685L）與「元大台灣50正2」（00631L）分別以74.2萬張及51.1萬張名列第二、三名；「元大台灣50」（0050）則以31.1萬張位居第四，成交金額達341億元。

此外，名列前十名的ETF還包括第五名的「主動統一台股增長」（00981A，30.4萬張）、第六名「凱基台灣TOP50」（009816，29.8萬張）、第八名「主動統一升級50」（00403A，25.2萬張）、第九名避險性質的「元大台灣50反1」（00632R，19.6萬張），以及第十名的「群益半導體收益」（00927，17.5萬張）。面板大廠友達（2409）則以25.9萬張成交量排名第七，成為唯一擠進前十名的非ETF個別股票。

個別權值股方面，護國神山台積電早盤一度下探至2420元、大跌70元，盤中跌幅收斂至2435元；聯發科重挫270元至4205元；台達電下挫155元至1630元；鴻海則下跌4.5元，收在238.5元。

傳統產業龍頭台塑四寶同步面臨拋售壓力，南亞與台化盤中雙雙跌停，股價分別來到314.5元及77元；台塑與台塑化也重挫7%至9%不等，分別下探至80.8元與111.5元。

news.Title: 不擔心台股重挫影響買氣　吳昕陽：目前業績優於預期
news.Content:
（中央社記者何秀玲台北15日電）台股今天盤中重挫逾千點，不過新光三越副董事長吳昕陽對於週年慶買氣仍信心十足。他表示，今年有寶可夢IP加持，包括台北南西店在內的首波週年慶表現優於預期，截至目前業績約成長3%，因此看好接下來第二波週年慶買氣。

新光三越台北信義新天地週年慶今天登場，吳昕陽出席為品牌加油打氣。新光三越表示，今天信義店首日來客比去年同期多2倍，開店前人潮即湧入千人，信義4館業績目標新台幣63.8億元，預計年增3%。

吳昕陽表示，看到今天週年慶人潮很高興，也讓他對業績達標有信心；首波6店週年慶都有達到業績目標，其中去年復業的台中店表現也不錯，「人氣、買氣都回來了」。首波業績截至目前約成長3%。

觀察週年慶消費型態變化，他指出，過去消費者排隊主要為搶購化妝品，如今更重視商品的特殊性及獨有性，例如上週寶可夢限量商品就吸引消費者排隊，消費型態確實出現改變。

對於今天台股盤中大跌逾千點，是否影響消費買氣。吳昕陽表示，他認為不會影響，目前週年慶買氣氣氛不錯，「到現在為止都有照著預期走」。

至於週年慶對第4季營運的挹注，吳昕陽表示，週年慶是第4季營運的一部分，後續還有耶誕節等消費商機，因此不會單獨以週年慶業績表現進一步看待第4季營運。（編輯：潘羿菁）1151015

news.Title: 韓股重挫　KOSPI、KOSDAQ雙雙觸發熔斷
news.Content:
（中央社首爾2026年10月15日綜合外電報導）韓國股市今天暴跌，韓國綜合股價指數（KOSPI）與以科技、生技等中小型成長企業為主的韓國創業板指（KOSDAQ）接連觸發第一階段熔斷機制。

韓國「中央日報」引述韓國交易所（KRX）消息，當地時間今天中午12時38分，KOSPI觸發第一階段熔斷機制。當時KOSPI指數較前一交易日下跌480.76點（跌幅8.0%），報5528.05點。

稍早12時23分13秒，KOSDAQ先觸發第一階段熔斷機制。觸發時KOSDAQ指數較前一交易日下跌66.00點（跌幅8.01%)，報757.88點。

第一階段熔斷機制在KOSPI或KOSDAQ指數較前一交易日跌8%以上並持續1分鐘下觸發。觸發後交易立即暫停20分鐘，除撤單報價外，新的報價申報也會停止。此後經過10分鐘的單一價格競價交易，再恢復正常交易。

KOSDAQ觸發第一階段熔斷機制，是自7月29日以來時隔約2個半月的首次。

KOSPI在當地時間上午9時7分觸發賣方程式交易暫停機制（Sidecar），KOSDAQ也於9時12分採取同樣措施。之後兩指數的跌幅超過8%，進而觸發熔斷。

美國通膨高於預期，市場對於聯準會（Fed）升息以及AI融資困境擔憂加深，全球科技硬體股拋售潮今天延燒至亞洲，韓股早盤開盤就重挫。

華爾街日報指出，美股納斯達克指數與標普500指數今雙雙創下7月以來的最大單日跌幅，主因為通膨隱憂與人工智慧（AI）板塊的不安情緒重創市場。

美國勞工部公布的最新報告顯示，9月核心消費者物價指數（CPI）月增0.3%，高於經濟學家預期的0.2%。超乎預期的火熱通膨數據引發對利率前景的擔憂。

而投資人對部分人工智慧（AI）概念股的戒心日深，出於包括擔憂中國競爭的威脅及借貸成本攀升等各項因素，盤中大舉出脫如CoreWeave和甲骨文（Oracle）等個股。

news.Title: 〈焦點股〉台股重挫逾千點 電信三雄成資金避風港紛紛走揚
news.Content:
台股今(15)日狂瀉超過1700點，資金流往電信三雄避風頭，中華電信(2412-TW)、台灣大(3045-TW)以及遠傳(4904-TW)紛紛走揚，其中，中華電信及台灣大股價創高，遠傳則挑戰前高。

中華電信盤中最高漲至154元，漲逾3%，台灣大衝上133元，漲逾4%，雙雙創歷史新天價，遠傳最高則漲至113元，漲幅超過4%，挑戰前高113.5元，電信三雄成交皆爆量超過1萬張。

電信三雄電信本業同步受惠蘋果新機iPhone 18 Pro系列開賣，9月營收與獲利表現亮麗，其中，中華電信因資產活化效益發酵，認列相關營收，9月每股純益0.57元，續坐單月獲利王寶座，中華電信指出，資產活化策略將聚焦「以租代售」為核心，以利持續貢獻持續性收入。

電信三雄前三季財務表現皆亮眼，中華電信稅後純益329.7億元，年增12.1%，每股純益4.25元；台灣大稅後純益129.5億元，年增22.87%，每股純益4.26元；遠傳稅後純益113.92億元，年增13.24%，每股純益3.16元。台灣大與中華電信前三季每股純益僅差0.01元，台灣大則成為前三季獲利王。

news.Title: 亞股恐慌殺盤！台股盤中摔逾1,800點，電子股面估值修正
news.Content:
【財訊快報／黃冠豪】亞股今早慘跌！受美國9月消費者物價指數（CPI）年增3.7%、高於市場預期影響，聯準會升息疑慮再起，加上美股費城半導體指數重挫4.3%，亞洲科技股今全面面臨沉重賣壓，台股開盤隨即出現恐慌性殺盤。韓國股市跌勢最為猛烈，KOSPI指數盤中一度重挫逾8%，跌至5,500點附近，觸發程式交易暫停機制。三星電子盤中下跌約9%，SK海力士跌逾11%，反映全球記憶體與AI半導體股遭到資金撤出。日本日經225指數同步走弱，盤中跌幅擴大至5%以上，失守65,000點，半導體設備與科技權值股成為主要賣壓來源。

台灣加權指數開低後賣壓迅速擴大，盤中最低下探46,795點，櫃買指數跌幅近6%，中小型電子股跌勢更為明顯。

權值股盤中全面承壓，台積電(2330)盤中跌至2,440元，跌幅2.01%；聯發科(2454)跌至4,150元，重挫7.26%；聯電(2303)跌至132.5元，跌幅6.69%；大立光(3008)一度跌至6,550元，跌幅4.80%。半導體及高價電子股成為法人提款重心。

熱門族群方面，被動元件延續昨日反彈後面臨獲利了結，國巨(2327)跌幅達9%，市場關注華新科(2492)、凱美(2375)能否守住短線支撐。PCB及CCL族群同樣遭遇調節，金像電(2368)跌逾7%，台光電(2383)下挫9%，聯茂(6213)跌逾8%，台燿(6274)同步。ABF載板族群賣壓沉重，欣興(3037)盤中重挫跌停，南電(8046)下跌6.99%，反映AI供應鏈高評價個股持續修正。矽光子與光通訊方面，聯亞(3081)下跌7.5%，光聖(6442)下跌8.5%，華星光(4979)下跌8%，即使800G、1.6T高速光通訊長期需求仍受市場看好，短線也難逃資金撤出壓力。

今日盤面最大變數是下午登場的台積電第三季法說會，市場關注AI需求、第四季財測、先進封裝產能及資本支出展望。短線台股須觀察47,000點支撐，以及48,000點能否重新站穩。若美債殖利率持續攀升、外資賣壓未見收斂，即使AI基本面未明顯轉弱，電子股仍可能面臨估值修正，操作宜保守，避免過早追逐反彈。

news.Title: Apple's Annual Revenue Quadrupled From $108 Billion to $416 Billion During Tim Cook's 15 Years as CEO, With iPhone Sales Alone Jumping From $47 Billion to Nearly $210 Billion. What That Growth Says About Betting on Apple's Next Chapter Under John Ternus.
news.Content:
Tim Cook unquestionably had a stellar run at the head of Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL). When he took over the CEO job in August 2011, Apple was already a force -- the iPhone was a hit, the iPad was relatively new, and the customer base was fiercely loyal.

But what Cook did over the next 15 years was remarkable . Apple's annual revenue nearly quadrupled, growing from $108 billion in fiscal 2011 to $416 billion in fiscal 2025. And iPhone sales, which were already enormous when Cook arrived, climbed from roughly $47 billion to nearly $210 billion.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Now John Ternus has taken over as Apple's CEO. And investors have an interesting question to consider: Can he build on Cook's success, or has Apple already experienced its greatest years of growth?

Tim Cook turned Apple into a much bigger business

Cook didn't invent the iPhone. But he deserves considerable credit for turning it into one of the most successful consumer products in history. Under his leadership, Apple expanded the iPhone's availability worldwide while introducing new models at different price points. That helped the company reach more customers without abandoning its premium pricing strategy.

Apple also expanded its lucrative services business, which includes the App Store, Apple Music, iCloud, and Apple Pay. Those products generate recurring revenue from customers who are already using Apple's devices, and they can be extremely profitable -- and they come without the overhead of developing new hardware product lines.

Apple's services segment generated $30.74 billion in revenue during its fiscal third quarter of 2026 (ending June 27), with a gross margin exceeding 75%.

Cook also used Apple's enormous cash flow to repurchase shares, helping increase earnings per share and rewarding long-term shareholders.

What John Ternus inherited

Ternus, who became CEO on Sept. 1, has a different challenge than Cook faced in 2011.

Apple already has more than 2.5 billion active devices worldwide, giving it an enormous customer base for new products and services. But expanding a company generating more than $400 billion in annual revenue isn't nearly as easy as growing a smaller business.

And Apple has been playing catch-up in artificial intelligence (AI).

The company introduced an upgraded Siri AI assistant earlier this year, hoping to make artificial intelligence a more useful part of its devices. On Oct. 13, Apple unveiled HomeView, a $299 smart home display that uses Siri AI to compete with products from Amazon and Alphabet .

Story Continues

But investors shouldn't expect another fourfold increase in annual revenue simply because Cook accomplished it. Apple's enormous size makes that a much more difficult proposition.

For Ternus, the opportunity isn't necessarily to duplicate Cook's growth. It's about finding new ways to make Apple's massive customer base even more valuable -- and giving shareholders a reason to stay invested for the next chapter.

news.Title: 台股重挫電信股成避風港　中華電、台灣大股價攻新高
news.Content:

news.Title: 搶到字節跳動大單也沒用？聯發科慘摔315元苦吞7連黑 分析師喊話：未來夢很大
news.Content: 聯發科（2454）繼 Google 之後，傳出可望再添AI重量級大戶「字節跳動」（TikTok 母公司），但利多消息未能帶動股價，反倒持續走弱。聯發科今（15）日開低走低，盤中重挫315元，最低下探至4,160元，不僅創下逾一個月以來新低 ...
news.AI_Summary:
• 聯發科傳出將為字節跳動（TikTok母公司）供應客製化資料中心晶片，但股價仍持續走弱，已連續7個交易日下跌。

news.Title: Meta Reports on Oct. 21. I'd Consider Buying the Stock Before It Does.
news.Content:
Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) will report its third-quarter results after the market closes on Wednesday, Oct. 21. Shares are at about $743 as I write -- roughly 6% under the stock's record close of $790, set in August 2025.

The stock has also gained about 30% since Aug. 31.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

The earnings figure in the report might look stunning. Analysts expect earnings per share of $6.77, according to FactSet, compared to just $1.05 a year ago.

But last year's number was distorted by a one-time charge. I'd buy the stock before the report anyway, though not because of a sixfold jump in earnings. What counts more is what the update says about Meta's ad business and its massive artificial intelligence (AI) budget.

Image source: Getty Images.

A distorted comparison

Meta's third-quarter 2025 earnings included a one-time, non-cash income tax charge of $15.9 billion linked to the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. Without it, Meta said its diluted earnings per share would've been $7.25 rather than $1.05.

Against that $7.25, FactSet's $6.77 estimate is around 7% lower. The gap probably reflects higher spending. Management also expects a tax rate of 15% to 17% for the rest of 2026, over the 14% Meta would've paid in the year-ago quarter without the charge.

Put another way, investors shouldn't read much into a big jump in earnings per share on Oct. 21.

Ad growth needs to hold up

Showing the strength of demand for Meta's ads, advertising revenue climbed 33% year over year in the first quarter of 2026. In the second quarter, ad revenue rose 27% to $59.4 billion. And management's guidance points to further deceleration. Meta expects third-quarter revenue of $61 billion to $64 billion -- growth of around 19% to 25% from $51.2 billion a year ago.

What would I like to see? Revenue in the top half of that range would be a solid start. But what's behind the growth matters even more.

In the second quarter, ad impressions rose 14% year over year, and the average price per ad was up 12%. CFO Susan Li tied the higher prices partly to stronger ad performance, plus improving economic conditions and currency.

Meta also said its AI-driven upgrades to its ad-ranking system led to an 8% boost in ad clicks and a 16% lift in conversions on Facebook in the quarter. If the average price per ad keeps rising at a double-digit rate in the third quarter, it suggests advertisers are paying more for ads that work better for them.

Story Continues

Can ads keep paying for the AI build-out?

The other half of the report is spending. Meta expects 2026 capital expenditures (including principal payments on finance leases) of $130 billion to $145 billion, up from $72.2 billion in 2025. Through June, it had spent $50.9 billion. Even the bottom of the range implies about $79 billion for the second half, or roughly $40 billion a quarter, up from $31.1 billion in the second quarter.

That spending is already hitting cash flow. Free cash flow dropped to just $784 million in the second quarter, versus $8.5 billion a year before. And long-term debt rose to $83.7 billion as of June 30, from $58.7 billion at year-end 2025.

Third-quarter free cash flow could slip below zero. A year ago, it was $10.6 billion.

Investors might also get a first look at 2027. A year ago, management used its third-quarter earnings call to say capital expenditure dollar growth would be "notably larger" in 2026 than in 2025. In July, Li held off on a 2027 number.

"Infrastructure planning remains highly dynamic and even this year, there are a range of outcomes embedded in our outlook," she said on the second-quarter earnings call.

I can live with a weak free cash flow quarter if ad revenue keeps growing at roughly 20% or higher. After all, Meta still expects its 2026 operating income to be above 2025's $83.3 billion. A far bigger 2027 spending plan paired with ad growth falling below that rate, though, might make me rethink the stock.

Of course, the report may push the stock down, especially after its climb since late August. But at around 22 times expected 2027 earnings, I think shares are reasonably priced for a company whose ad sales rose 27% last quarter. At that price, Meta doesn't need a blowout quarter -- just revenue growth in management's range and a spending plan the ad business can cover.

Overall, I'd consider buying shares ahead of the report. But, given the risks, probably gradually rather than all at once.

news.Title: MongoDB lets apps pay only for what they use
news.Content:
Nobody thinks about the database behind their banking app until it freezes, usually on the busiest days. To stay ready, many companies pay all year for capacity they need on a handful of days.

MongoDB Inc. (MDB) wants to break that habit. On Tuesday, Sept. 29, 2026, it launched Atlas Infinite, which bills customers only for the computing and storage they use, according to a press release .

Okta Inc. (OKTA), a login provider, said the option will let it handle surges "without paying for idle resources." Infinite is still in public preview.

A day before the launch, MongoDB revealed that CEO CJ Desai had left for a senior role at Meta Platforms Inc. (META). Desai lasted under a year, and former chief Dev Ittycheria is back as interim CEO.

On Tuesday, Oct. 13, 2026, Wolfe Research flagged the exits of Chief Customer Officer Erica Volini, along with Pablo Stern-Plaza, chief product officer for AI and emerging products. Neither appears on MongoDB's leadership page .

Revenue hit $771.8 million in the quarter ended Friday, July 31, 2026, up 30% from a year earlier, according to MongoDB's earnings release .

Also read: MongoDB stock crashes 26% as its CEO jumps ship

Atlas, the cloud service Infinite plugs into, made up about 73% of it, the release shows. "It is business as usual at MongoDB," CFO Mike Berry told investors the day Infinite debuted.

Most of MongoDB's revenue depends on how much customers use it, according to a Bank of America research note shared with TheStreet. Infinite gives them a cheaper way to do the same work. The note calls the CEO change the key immediate risk, but pricing will matter longer.

After hosting a group call with MongoDB's investor relations chief, BofA analyst Koji Ikeda kept his Buy rating and $540 price target.

The report, dated Tuesday, Oct. 13, 2026, is titled "AI strategy intact, near-term debate is execution; Reiterate Buy." Its bear case warns that Infinite "compresses Atlas spend through improved efficiency."

Customers pocket the savings before MongoDB sees growth

Infinite separates computing from storage, so each can grow on its own. In internal tests, it delivered 189% more throughput per dollar than the standard service, the release said. The same work can cost far less.

Management says customers will spend those savings on more work. Chief product officer Ben Cefalo cited the Jevons paradox, the 19th-century finding that efficient steam engines made Britain burn more coal.

Okta is buying the savings, while Cefalo is selling the growth. Although savings show up on the next bill, extra usage takes years to earn.

Story Continues

The savings could come out of MongoDB's sales

The note's other debate is whether MongoDB's document database stays different enough from PostgreSQL.

Developers already lean toward that rival. PostgreSQL drew 57.9% of respondents to the database question in Stack Overflow's 2026 Developer Survey , versus 19% for MongoDB.

Wolfe said the exits came faster than expected. Selling a new way to pay takes steady customer relationships, and the customer chief is gone.

Analysts say Buy MongoDB but disagree on what it's worth

MongoDB carries a consensus Buy rating from 40 analysts with an average price target of $449.74 , according to StockAnalysis . All five of the latest calls are Buys, yet their targets sit $155 apart.

Stifel Financial analyst Brad Reback cut his target price to $385 from $465 on Sunday, Oct. 4, 2026, a week after the CEO's exit. Bank of America's $540 is the highest.

Wolfe's Alex Zukin held his target at $440 on Tuesday, Oct. 13, 2026. Bank of Nova Scotia analyst Patrick Colville lifted his target to $450 on Thursday, Oct. 8, 2026. Daniel Ives of Yorkville Ives & Co. started at $430 a day earlier.

On the day of the note, shares jumped as much as 7.9% before closing about 2.2% lower. Wolfe's comments on the exits surfaced that afternoon. Shares remain about 21% below their August peak of $473.10.

More Bank of America:

BofA splits software into winners and losers as AI agents arrive

Bank of America reveals hidden moat that makes Morgan Stanley a buy

Bank of America resets Amazon stock forecast on delivery plan

Bank of America thinks MongoDB's bet has room to run

Ikeda raised his fiscal 2028 revenue estimate by 3% to $3.65 billion and his fiscal 2029 estimate by 6% to $4.39 billion , according to the note.

Before the investor day, I flagged the growth target as the number to watch. Management raised it to 20% or more a year from the high teens, as its investor day presentation shows.

Bank of America raised its Atlas forecasts yet sees growth slowing to 24% in fiscal 2028 and 23% in fiscal 2029. That compares with 27% in the year ending January 2027. Even the bull is not modeling a surge from Infinite.

For app users, the payoff could be fewer freezes on busy days. PicPay, a Brazilian payments app, handled four times its normal peak traffic for two hours with zero failures, MongoDB said. It is still early, so don't count on it everywhere this holiday season.

The note's bull case is that Infinite wins new AI and agent workloads, while its bear case is that cheaper usage shrinks Atlas spending. Ikeda sides with the bulls, arguing that "AI and modernization support durable growth."

BofA will judge it by Atlas growth and existing customers' spending. As the cloud shifts to pay-per-use, MongoDB will test whether cheaper computing grows a supplier's sales or just its customers' savings.

news.Title: Inside the Intel Supreme Court Case: Fees, Fiduciaries and Hidden Risk
news.Content:
In this episode of the Broadcast Retirement Network, we sit down with Chris Tobe, CFA, CAIA, Chief Investment Officer at The Hackett Group and author of "Kentucky Fried Pensions," to unpack the Intel Supreme Court case and what it means for everyday retirement savers.

Transcript:

Jeffrey Snyder, Broadcast Retirement Network

We're gonna welcome back to the program, Chris Tobe of the Hackett Group. Chris, it's always great to see you.

Thanks for joining us in the program again this morning.

Chris Tobe, CFA, CAIA, Chief Investment Officer at The Hackett Group

Great, I always enjoy it, Jeff, and I enjoy your daily newsletter every morning as well.

And thank you for being a long-term subscriber and for your willingness to come on. Chris, I always like talking about, I like different perspectives. I think that what this show is about, candidly, and if I were to give my opinion, is about bringing all perspectives so that people have the most information they can to make the best decision possible.

So what I like about your perspective in particular is that you have served on many boards. You've written books about being on those boards, and you've also looked at a lot of the legal cases around retirement plan litigation. So with that context in mind, I had reached out to you because I wanna talk about the Intel case that's currently in front of the Supreme Court.

Give us the lay of the land here because we've talked to you about fees. This isn't necessarily about fees. It's about something else.

Well, again, that's the issue. I think it really should be about fees and is, but it's being pushed to be kind of this generic performance type of issue, which I think is used to cover up excessive fees. So that's part of my whole issue here.

And I don't like the way the defense attorneys or the plaintiff attorneys are kind of handling this case and talking about it. The thing about a meaningful benchmark, when you have things like target date funds, and this is what Intel has done is they have a lot of future mega plans like Intel and GM, they'll have what we call master trust where they'll have this, it's kind of like the target date fund we see everywhere else where they put stocks, bonds, private equity, hedge, all their different asset classes in one kind of master trust. And they use it for both their defined benefit plans and their defined contribution plans. So the Intel has, I think it's a private acreage hedge fund buried inside this master trust.

Story Continues

And again, performance, to me, it's all about transparency here, being able to see down to the asset class level. So remember right now in 401k plans, over 50% of the assets are now in what we call target date or kind of asset allocation structures. But what we don't, so with all those assets, and each of those have four or five different asset classes or maybe more underneath them.

And the whole problem to me is that the industry has used these target date funds actually to be able to block the transparency of the underlying funds. So that you see a target date fund and you don't know what its allocation is. You don't know what the fees are underneath individually.

Sometimes you'll have an aggregate. So by reporting everything in aggregate, I think we leave out all the transparency. And this is what I think Intel's more about than the actual performance around meaningful benchmarks, which is a term that has no, to me, I've never heard investments before.

I think it's made up by Wall Street attorneys to block transparency, this whole term of meaningful benchmark. Because I was taught, okay, I'm sorry, go ahead.

Finish your thought that I have a follow-up to that because I wanna get into your role as a professional. So finish your thought and then I'll come back to you with a question.

So how do you benchmark something? First of all, the classic benchmark would be the S&P 500 index versus a large cap stock fund. And in that type of benchmark, we know what the benchmark is.

We know what the underlying securities are in both of what we're investing in and what the index is. But for a contract like a private equity, private credit, or even annuity, there's no underlying securities to measure. It's just a contract.

And first of all, I have a very hard time benchmarking any contracts. And then you have a target date that has three contracts and three funds in it, mixing and matching them creates very difficult, lots of difficulty in benchmarking. So yeah, go ahead.

Okay, so my follow-up is, let's talk about your role as a fiduciary. Because one of the things you do in addition to serving as a witness for the plaintiff, right? So why is this transparency important for the work you do as a fiduciary?

As someone who is advising the plan sponsor who owns the plan, runs the plan, has a responsibility to pay out benefits from the plan. What does that mean to you as that individual?

If I don't have transparency down to the fund level in a target date fund, how can I have any fiduciary control over the underlying assets? If I'm not allowed to know the fees, I don't know how they're computing performance, that to me as a fiduciary, it's a black hole. And black holes create liability for me as a fiduciary, the plan and everyone else, when there's not transparency all the way down to the asset class level in these types of funds.

So I wanna play devil's advocate. Well, maybe not advocate, but the accountancy of that would be, there's a fun fact sheet. But let's talk about the fun fact sheet that, so every targeted fund, every fund in a retirement plan, has this fun fact sheet.

It's meant to distill what is arguably a very complex product into something that is meaningful to the end user. So is that enough for the participant or for you to look at? So that one or two pager, that's a PDF that's available for download.

Well, for participants, it's hard to get them to read more than one page anyhow, and it's maybe not fair to have them do that. But what I'm looking for, and I'm actually maybe pushing legislation around this, is that on the 5500 form, which everyone can have access to, a fiduciary should be looking at, the plan should be looking at, and a participant, if they want to, can go to the 5500 form, then there should be more disclosures and transparencies there. The fun fact sheet, it's just gonna be very difficult to get that level of transparency there without making it too complicated and something that a participant wouldn't read anyhow.

So let's go back to the Intel case. So this has been going on, this has wound its way through the court system. Again, you and I are not attorneys, although you have acted as a witness in several litigation cases.

So you have more experience than I am. So where does this wind up? Because the end of the Supreme Court term is in June, right?

So they had to write, they've been taking, having hearings from both sides. I won't pretend to have listened to those conversations. It's a little too nuanced for me.

But where does this wind its way through, come June of 27, or does it, do we get some kind of decision in 27?

I think whatever decision we get is probably gonna be murky. Because it's all about these kind of, these lawyers like to talk about all this procedural things. And it's all about can, when you file a case, will there be discovery, all about issues of level of transparency that the plaintiffs can ask for.

And it's just gonna be positioning around all those type of issues around whether you can file a case, do you have enough to file and get past the motion to dismiss? So a lot of it, again, revolves around those issues. And I think at the end of this, it may be kind of a, the Supreme Court will say, well, yeah, you need to have some, it'll be a mixed opinion that may not tell us anything and that we'll still be in limbo.

And that's why I think we need some better disclosure legislation out there to really fix this. I don't think the Supreme Court, they're kind of, the way they're looking at and talking about meaningful benchmarks and things like that, the Supreme Court just doesn't have the ability to look down in the detail level. I mean, it would take them 20 years to get inside these things.

It's just, they have to rule on kind of some, the more superficial legal questions around discovery and things like that. But I don't think it will really solve it either way come June, whatever their decision is, because I don't know what kind of decision they could make. They can't just say, oh, private equity is great.

And you have no discretion. They're still gonna hold up ERISA, but how they do it and what's the threshold for litigation is really what this is going to set. And it could be higher or lower threshold for litigation, but your largest plans will still, and again, I think the plaintiff attorneys are guilty of this.

They tend to go after the mega plans, the top couple hundred of them for about anything.

Yeah, well, that's where the candidly, that's where the money is, right? If you're a lawyer and you're looking to get paid, those small plans don't probably pay us.

Well, I still think the medium sized plans, a hundred million to a billion, those plans still are good. Good, and that's where I think more of the solid cases are anyhow. But the mega plans, they're also easier to find plaintiffs.

It's hard to find, you have to find plaintiffs because most plaintiffs, no one understands these plans, especially the plaintiffs. So getting plaintiffs is also a challenge for those attorneys as well. So that's kind of where I'm going.

Well, let me ask you about, so when we had you on, I don't know, a couple of months ago, we talked about these new Department of Labor rules. I haven't seen the final version of it. I've seen the, I guess the proposed and then they got the comments, et cetera.

We talked to you during the comment period or after the comment period. So when do these, does this have an impact on those rules and do you have a sense for when those rules might be released? I mean, that you would think they would have been, how long to take to finalize rules?

I don't know. A lot of these rules are not real hard and fast things. There's kind of loose gotten.

You said, you can have private equity, but you still have to do your due diligence and do all the types of things that ERISA requires. And I think what it may do is it may embolden the industry, especially to put a lot of private equity things in small plans, but the larger plans will still stay away because there's litigation risk. So you've got like two parts of the market here.

It probably may not be enough though that large plans will invest, but small plans, especially under a hundred million who have really no risk of litigation, it'll start growing in those areas with the DOL guys. But then when we get to change parties and go to another DOL, it could flip around in that direction as well.

And so to that point, and I don't want to get, we don't do politics on the show, but if there is a switch in the executive branch or in the Congress, could whatever is written be done? So for example, ESG, that was a big proponent or a big initiative, environmental social governance funds were a big initiative in the last administration. That appears to have been in some ways unwound.

So could what we're talking about today be, even if the Supreme Court rules and we have these new regs, couldn't that be undone?

Well, kind of, I mean, it can be a shifting back and forth. The ES, I think ESG is mostly a bunch of noise in my opinion. And again, some ESG funds charge too high fees.

And I don't like, I don't think, I think even violate the governance part of themselves because they charge higher fees with these ESG funds. So there's a lot of hypocrisy in every side. And when you get ESG kind of try to throw politics in here and it tends to be messy on both sides, going back and forth.

And I really don't think from a material point of view, it makes that much difference. And the private equity will probably start out small as well inside of target date funds. And as we go along here, these are not gonna be monster issues right away.

They're just gonna kind of gradually kind of move over time.

Yeah, it's gonna be interesting to see. You know, like I said, I just kind of follow it from the outside looking in. It'll be interesting to see what you're talking about, but also what materially it means to the end user, to the participant.

Is it going to increase the return? Is it going, now, you know, everyone always says, oh yeah, well, if you add this sliver, it's gonna do X, Y, Z, create greater diversification, a greater return. I think time will tell as to whether or not that makes sense.

And it'll be a, you know, it'll give people, plant sponsors the reason to say, hey, should we keep our plan plain vanilla? Anyway, TBD, Chris, it's always great to see you. Thanks for popping by the program, sharing your expertise.

And we look forward to having you back on the program again very soon, sir.

Great, Jeff. Thanks for having me.

news.Title: Elon Musk takes a direct swipe at Broadcom CEO and AI investors
news.Content:
Elon Musk rarely passes up a chance at a one-liner. When Broadcom CEO Hock Tan compared many AI investors to casino gamblers, Musk replied on X to a post summarizing the remarks with five words: "No crying in the casino."

The jab added fuel to a growing debate over how long the AI boom can last.

The exchange landed at a touchy moment for the AI trade. The Nasdaq fell 1.25% on Oct. 8 as chip stocks, including Nvidia (NVDA) and Broadcom (AVGO), took a hit after questions surfaced about OpenAI's revenue.

Also read: AT&T CEO holds firm stance on Elon Musk's SpaceX phone strategy

Hock Tan says many AI investors are gambling

Tan made the comments on Oct. 12 at the DBS Asia Future Forward Conference in Singapore, sharing the stage with Intel (INTC) CEO Lip-Bu Tan on a panel moderated by DBS CEO Tan Su Shan.

"A lot of investors have no clue what they are investing in," he said , adding that some set very extreme expectations "only to find out that it's almost like they are in a casino."

He was just as blunt about corporate spending.

"People are just wasting money, spending tokens, trying to understand (AI)," Tan said , comparing companies to a child who burns through $10 of arcade tokens in minutes and learns nothing.

He added that OpenAI's annualized revenue of roughly $50 billion was "by itself, not that bad" for a startup.

That OpenAI figure is exactly what rattled the market a few days earlier. OpenAI told investors its annualized revenue was approaching $50 billion at the end of September, well below the nearly $70 billion figure that had been widely reported, and AI infrastructure stocks fell on Oct. 8.

Musk has played both sides of this debate. In September, he said Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei was "right" after Amodei called for an intentional slowdown in advanced AI development.

Tan brushed that push aside, saying on Sept. 14 that the debate had not changed Broadcom's AI forecasts "in the least."

Broadcom is cashing in on the boom it's warning about

Tan's warning carries extra weight because few companies have gained more from AI spending than Broadcom.

Broadcom reported fiscal third-quarter revenue of $29.6 billion in early September, slightly ahead of analyst estimates, with AI semiconductor revenue up 221% from a year earlier, according to its SEC filing . It guided for $21.7 billion in fourth-quarter AI chip revenue, yet shares still fell after hours.

The longer-term targets are even bigger.

Broadcom expects AI semiconductor revenue of about $115 billion in fiscal 2027 and about $230 billion in fiscal 2028. Tan also arranged a financing partnership with Apollo and Blackstone to back more than 20 gigawatts of computing capacity, a buildout that will require hundreds of billions of dollars.

Story Continues

That financing angle is where Tan sees the real squeeze.

"What I think might be the biggest constraint is capital," he said in Singapore, while Lip-Bu Tan pointed to "capital and the cost of capital." Hock Tan also said computing demand could outrun supply through 2029 or 2030, according to Benzinga .

Broadcom is deeply tied to that money chase. Broadcom has been seeking more than $50 billion in financing tied to OpenAI as tech companies race to buy chips and expand AI infrastructure.

The bill for the AI buildout keeps growing

The spending numbers explain why capital is suddenly the main topic. The largest U.S. hyperscalers are on track to spend roughly $800 billion on capital projects this year, and Goldman Sachs projects $1.2 trillion in capital expenditure in 2027, as reported by TheStreet .

Wall Street has been warning about this for months. Morgan Stanley said in February that hyperscaler AI spending was "set to exceed dot-com era telecom capex in both magnitude and length." Its bear case was that "investment outpaces monetization for several years."

More Artificial Intelligence:

AI's biggest business opportunity may not look like AI

AI racks are outgrowing old power: 2 chipmakers have a strategy

BofA splits software into winners and losers as AI agents arrive

The borrowing is already showing up in bond markets. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said in September that hyperscalers raising money is part of why Treasury yields have climbed, adding that "the competition for capital is real," according to Fortune .

Morgan Stanley expects global AI-related debt issuance to approach $570 billion this year.

Even AI believers are getting nervous about the price tag. The Financial Times reported that Big Tech firms are using guarantees to back as much as $300 billion in debt tied to AI data centers and chips.

SoftBank also raised $11.1 billion in one of the biggest high-yield bond deals ever to fund its OpenAI investment.

What investors should watch next

The cost of money is the first thing to track. The 10-year Treasury yield hit its 2026 peak of 5.37% on Oct. 7, its highest level since March 2002, which raises the bar for every project funded with borrowed money.

The biggest spenders still look well protected. The largest hyperscalers have shown little sensitivity to higher funding costs so far, while smaller and highly leveraged businesses are more exposed.

Musk, for his part, has his own chips on the table. SpaceX went public in June in what was billed as the largest IPO in history, and it absorbed xAI earlier this year. The company says xAI built the first gigawatt-scale AI training cluster.

For investors watching from the sidelines, the question is who walks away from this casino with winnings.

Related: Broadcom CEO echoes Warren Buffett with warning for investors

news.Title: 台積電法說會前報喜！艾司摩爾營收年增55% 財測第三度上調
news.Content:
台積電（2330）今（15）日盤後將舉辦法說會，合作夥伴艾司摩爾（ASML）則搶先公布財報，本季業績預測優於市場預期，全年展望更是第三度上調，ASML表示，未來兩年擴產計劃仍難以完全滿足市場需求。

根據ASML公布的資料，截至9月27日，第三季營收達116.62億歐元，年增幅高達55%，略高於市場預期；毛利率為57.5%，優於市場預估，連續五季提升。

ASML預估，第四季淨銷售將落在142億至152億歐元間，毛利率約57%，均超出市場預期；全年淨銷售將達440億至450億歐元，下限高於之前預測的430億歐元。

隨著半導體產能持續擴張，ASML曾預估2027年低數值孔徑極紫外光（Low NA EUV）產能將提升30%、2028年再增長30%。但執行長傅凱（Christophe Fouquet）表示，目前收到2028年大量訂單，加上客戶每日皆提出增加產能要求，原有產能規劃恐難以滿足需求。

傳凱補充，公司正積極尋求方法，提升2028年產能增幅至高於先前設定的30%，未來AI相關投資將帶動客戶對中長期設備需求預期提升，有客戶甚至對2029年、2030年的訂單表示興趣；彭博資訊分析師則認為，ASML最新財報釋出訊息，可能暗示台積電相關動向，目前台灣仍是ASML新款微影設備最大出貨地區。

news.Title: ByteDance in Talks to Secure MediaTek AI Chips for Data Centers
news.Content:
(Bloomberg) -- ByteDance Ltd. is close to an agreement to buy MediaTek Inc. data center semiconductors, a deal that would secure vital components for TikTok's owner while helping the Taiwanese chipmaker compete with Qualcomm Inc.

Most Read from Bloomberg

Stocks Fall on Inflation Woes as Chip Rout Deepens: Markets Wrap

Apple Unveils $299 HomeView Hub as Part of New Smart Home Push

Epic Games Delays Disney Project, Asks Developers to Use More AI

CoreWeave's Big Dream Crashes Into Reality as Yields Top 15%

CoreWeave's Bonds Turn Distressed, Drawing 'Yikes' From Musk

The Chinese social media company is in advanced talks with MediaTek over the supply of bespoke chips that will help run ByteDance data centers, people familiar with the matter said. The Taiwanese firm will provide an unspecified amount of Application Specific Integrated Circuits, or chips customized to work with a clients' platform, the people said, asking to remain anonymous to talk about a private arrangement. If the deal goes through, ByteDance may become MediaTek's second major customer for such ASICs, after Alphabet Inc.'s Google.

ByteDance is ramping up hardware spending to fuel a bet on AI as its next growth engine. But like Chinese rivals Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. and Tencent Holdings Ltd., it's barred from the most cutting-edge AI chips from the likes of Nvidia Corp. Local players such as Huawei Technologies Co. can't meet all demand.

China's biggest private firm is thus exploring alternatives including partnerships with chip designers — something that's allowed under current US export curbs so long as the AI computing power a Chinese firm is seeking doesn't exceed a certain threshold. ByteDance struck a similar deal with Qualcomm earlier this year to procure millions of AI chips, Bloomberg News reported.

For MediaTek, a large-scale contract win would boost its efforts to diversify away from mobile phones and compete with Qualcomm and Broadcom Inc. in data centers, an arena it's less familiar with. The Taiwanese firm expects its AI chip sales to reach about $2 billion this year and is targeting 15% of the $80 billion market next year. Nvidia announced a deal to invest $3.5 billion in the Hsinchu-based chipmaker in September, propelling those ambitions.

ByteDance didn't have immediate comment, while MediaTek representatives declined to comment.

MediaTek has emerged as a key beneficiary of a push by technology companies to design custom semiconductors for AI applications, using its expertise in mobile processors to participate in the data center infrastructure rush. With a market value of around $210 billion, it's Taiwan's biggest firm after Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.

Story Continues

ByteDance represents an opportunity for MediaTek: a high-volume customer that should galvanize the Taiwanese firm's foray into one of the fastest-growing segments of the semiconductor industry. Like the largest US firms, ByteDance and its Chinese rivals plan to ramp up spending on the infrastructure required to train and run AI services — in anticipation of widespread consumer adoption as the technology evolves.

The Beijing-based company is considering boosting capital spending to as much as $70 billion this year — more than double last year's total — to build out its data centers and other AI infrastructure. That may rise to $100 billion in 2027 next year, if economic and business conditions are favorable. It secured a $30 billion loan in September to fund its outlay.

ByteDance's spending marks a new, much more aggressive push to cement an early lead in key segments like chatbots and video, and expand its influence overseas. The company is pinning its AI business around flagship models like Seedance, which faces stiff competition from the likes of Alibaba's Happy Horse, Kuaishou Technology's Kling AI and Google.

--With assistance from Debby Wu and Zheping Huang.

news.Title: 散戶狂抄底0050正二、00685L！2小時內掃87萬張「正2」 分析師示警了
news.Content:
台股今（15）日在美股崩跌與外資觀望氣氛夾擊下呈低檔震盪，晶圓代工龍頭台積電（2330）盤中重挫，拖累大盤大跌，但是市場上卻有一股「越跌越買」的抄底資金湧入槓桿型商品，群益台灣加權正2（00685L）與元大台灣50正2（00631L）今日盤中雙雙爆出巨量，分別突破 52 萬張與 35 萬張，強勢擠進台股成交量排行榜前三名。

法說會前夕押寶落空 散戶轉戰「正2」搶反彈

台積電今日召開第三季法說會，雖然市場普遍預期其第四季營收與毛利率均有優異表現，但受到美CPI物價指數升溫與AI融資疑慮夾擊，台積電股價未見「押寶行情」，盤中一度重摔70元至2,420元，帶動加權指數同步拉回。

不過，市場資金顯然出現分歧。觀察盤中成交量能，買盤大舉轉向槓桿型 ETF，藉由兩倍放大的價格彈性進行短線卡位。

分析師：爆量不一定反轉

群益台灣加權正2（00685L）盤中成交量達52萬張、元大台灣50正2（00631L）也達35萬張，不過，倫元投顧分析師王春盛表示，「爆量不代表行情一定反轉」，也不等於逢低買進訊號，尤其兩檔都是正向2倍槓桿ETF，漲跌幅可能放大，長期持有還有每日重新平衡造成的複利偏差風險。操作上，短線投資人不宜因價格急跌就重押搶反彈，可先觀察台積電法說內容、加權指數止跌力道及成交量變化；已有持股者應檢視槓桿部位是否超出承受範圍，必要時分批減碼。正2較適合能密切盯盤、承受較大波動的投資人，不宜當作一般存股工具，務必設定停損並避免融資加碼。

受美國上(9)月通膨數據超乎預期影響，市場擔憂美國聯準會(Fed)進一步升息，導致AI科技股承壓，美股四大指數皆墨，亞股今(15)日一片哀嚎，台股也難以倖免，早盤重跌1,472點，指數最低一度下探47,153點，失守月線，盤面上僅資安、電信股表現較佳，盤中暫報47,179點，下跌1,482點或3.05%，單日成交量估1.69兆元。

電子權值股部分今日全面重挫，多檔跌破季線，下午法說即將登場的台積電(2330-TW)開低走低，開盤跌逾2.2%或70元，最低來到2,420元，失守月線；聯發科(2454-TW)重挫半根停版跌；台達電(2308-TW)跌7%、鴻海(2317-TW)跌1.85%；日月光投控(3711-TW)跌7.76%。

千金股受大盤拖累影響也全面重挫一片慘綠，旺矽(6669-TW)、緯穎(6669-TW)雙雙打入跌停板，僅藥華藥(6446-TW)、玉晶光(3406-TW)、大量(3167-TW)暫開紅盤上揚。

電信三雄部分股價堅挺上揚，中華電(2412-TW)漲逾2%以上、遠傳(4904-TW)漲3.2%、台灣大(3045-TW)漲3.16%。

資安股部分，意蘭(6925-TW)、驊宏姿(6148-TW)漲7%，華經(2468 -TW)、力新(5202-TW)上揚。

近日表現強於大盤的塑化股，今日也全面拉回修正，南亞(1303-TW)、台化(1326-TW)、國喬(1312-TW)跳水亮燈跌停版；台塑化(6505-TW)、台塑(1301-TW)重跌超過8%以上，台苯(1310-TW)、台達化(1309-TW)、台聚(1304-TW)跌逾半根跌停板。

法人表示，AI資金借貸成本上升隱憂，從債市蔓延至股市，加上中東局勢升溫 帶動油價反彈，Fed官員利率立場分歧，為市場帶來高度不確定性，投資人可關注下午台積電法說能否重拾AI信心。相關主流類股部分，投資人可關注PCB、被動元件、光通訊、石英元件、低軌衛星、塑膠類股。

美股周三(14日)表現部分，道瓊工業指數下跌48.62點或0.09%，收51,621.48點；標普500下跌86.51點或1.11%，收7,718.94點；那斯達克下跌511.51點或1.88%，收26,692.87點；費城指數重挫524.41點或4.3%，收11,684.38點。

news.Title: 散戶大軍搶買0050！不到1小時爆逾2000萬股
news.Content:
零股大軍搶買0050！權王台積電（2330）法說會前押寶行情落空，盤中大跌70元，卻意外引爆國民ETF元大台灣 50（0050）的抄底買氣。0050 開盤不到一小時便爆出 超過2000萬股的零股成交量，成交量還在持續擴大中。

美股周三（14日）主要指數全數收黑，其中那斯達克指數與費城半導體指數雙雙大跌逾 500 點；受美股利空波及，台指期夜盤重挫 853 點，拖累台北股市今（15）日開盤一度重挫逾 1,400 點。

權王台積電盤中一度大跌 70 元至 2,420 元，寫下今年第七大單日跌點。然而，隨著台積電股價拉回，反而激起國民 ETF「元大台灣 50（0050）」的零股搶購熱潮，開盤不到一小時便爆出 1,683 萬股零股成交量，以盤中價 109.55 元估算，吸金突破 18 億元，顯示散戶投資人正蜂湧進場撿便宜。

不只零股交易亮眼，0050 整張（大盤）成交量也迅速衝破17萬張，總成交金額超過180億元以上，交投相當熱絡。

倫元投顧分析師王春盛表示，受美國科技股重挫拖累，日本、南韓及台股早盤同步拉回，0050元大台灣50盤中成交量已逾16萬張，顯示市場交投熱絡，多空換手加劇。 由於0050高度連動台積電，今天下午台積電法說會將成為重要觀察指標，市場聚焦AI需求、先進製程及第四季展望。

王春盛也提到，操作上短線不宜只因成交量放大就認定是低檔買點，也不要急著重押法說行情，已持有者可觀察大盤止跌力道；想進場者建議分批布局，避免一次投入過多資金，若法說展望優於預期，仍須觀察市場是否買單；若利多不漲，則要留意賣壓延續，並預先設定可承受的停損或減碼條件。

大盤跌逾1400點，4檔ETF交投熱絡超越0050，主動中信台灣收益（00406A）成交量超過71萬張大量奪冠；群益台灣加權正2（00685L）43萬張居次；0050正二32萬張第三、瑤池金母的00981A逾17萬張第四名，0050則排第五。

在今日的ETF成交量排行榜中，奪下冠軍寶座的是主動型基金統一台股增長（00981A）成交量近34萬張；緊追在後的是有「不配息版 0050」之稱的凱基台灣 TOP50（009816），以29.7萬多張位居第二；第三名則是群益台灣精選高息（00919），成交量達27.6萬張。

陳依旻／財經特派記者副組長，主跑央行、證交所、投信投顧等

news.Title: 亞股集體重挫！韓股摔7%熔斷、日股跌4% 台股狂瀉1400點
news.Content:
受到美國通膨指數超預期、市場對加息的疑慮升溫，美股費半指數率先重挫4.3%，衝擊亞股今（15）日全面下跌，其中韓股跌幅最為嚴重，南韓KOSPI爆跌7%、觸發熔斷機制，日經指數則下跌逾2700點，跌幅4%，台股也慘摔1400點，失守48K，暫報47264點，跌幅2.82%。

由於美國9月消費者物價指數上升，美國聯準會可能進一步調高利率、帶動借貸成本上升，特別是對AI科技類股造成壓力，不安情緒在市場中蔓延，影響美股費半指數重挫4.3%、連六日收黑，那斯達克下跌1.88%，道瓊指數下跌0.09%，標普500下跌1.11%；台積電ADR也下跌3.4%。

亞洲股市受到美股衝擊，韓股一開盤就重摔，SK海力士跌逾10%、三星跌逾8%，盤中一度下挫至5546點，南韓KOSPI指數跌逾7%，觸發熔斷機制；日股同受影響，日經225指數盤中持續下挫，一度下跌2700點，跌幅逾4%，失守66000點大關。

台股今日早盤以48382點開出，盤中一度下挫逾1400點，觸及47153點低點，失守月線，預估成交量1.2兆，台積電下跌逾2%，聯發科跌逾5%，緯穎、南亞、台化跌停亮燈。

news.Title: 亞股也崩！日股急殺3600點 韓股重挫8%側車又熔斷 日韓ETF重挫逾9%
news.Content:
（13點53分更新）

亞股今（15）早又現史詩級崩跌走勢！日股急殺3651點之多，跌破6萬7、6萬6、6萬5千點共三大整數大關，寫9月底來最低，跌幅近5.4%，而韓股跌更重，今早一度大跌8.5%，更一度觸發側車機制，這已是二天內2度觸發，中午韓交所宣布第9度熔斷20分鐘。台股下午有護國神山台積電法說會，但今早沒逃過空方氣焰，急殺1655.96點，跌幅近3.41%，在亞股中跌幅未超越日韓。台灣掛牌日股ETF如台新半導體（00951）、中信半導體ETF（00954）一度重挫逾9.9~10.26%，大華韓國ETF009829跌逾9%。

美國通膨數據高於預期，美國9月消費者物價指數（CPI）年增率由8月的3.4%升至3.7%，引發市場對聯準會可能進一步升息的擔心，AI雲端族群CoreWeave狂瀉逾15%、美光重跌4.08%，台積電ADR也重跌3.4%。

美股大跌也引發亞股跟進急殺，日經225指數今早由66,880.37點、下跌8百多點開出，但跌幅迅速擴大，接連失守6萬7、6萬6，中場後連6萬5都守不住，最低跌到64092.74，跳水3651點之多。

韓國綜合股價指數（KOSPI）於15日開盤後不久，三星與海力士分別狂殺逾8%和超過11%，韓股大跌475點，直接跌破6千點，最低下探5497.27點，跌幅8.51%，連5500點都失守，韓股今年最高在9114點。

同時當KOSPI 200期貨跌幅達5%，觸發賣方側車「程式交易暫停機制」（sell-side sidecar）機制，暫停程式賣盤。這是2天內第2度觸發該機制，前一次發生於13日。側車機制用於阻斷股指期貨波動經由程序化交易傳導至現貨市場，僅臨時暫停同向程序交易申報，並非全市場停盤。

韓股早上側車 中午又熔斷

南韓證交所中午12時38分（台灣時間上午11時38分）又啟動「熔斷」機制，暫停交易20分鐘，這是韓股今年第9次啟動熔斷機制。

受日韓股市重挫影響，在台灣掛牌的日股與韓股ETF也同樣遭殃，其中以台新半半導體（00951）、中信半導體ETF（00954）重挫逾9.9~10.26%，大華韓國ETF009829跌逾9%最慘烈。

葉憶如／財經特派記者組長，主跑金管會、金控壽險、航空等

news.Title: 晶片股拋售延燒亞洲　韓股早盤重挫6%日股跌3%
news.Content:
（中央社東京2026年10月15日綜合外電報導）美國通膨高於預期，市場對於美國聯準會升息以及AI融資困境擔憂加深，全球科技硬體股拋售潮今天延燒至亞洲，韓股早盤重挫6%，日本日經指數也跌逾3%。

法新社報導，日股基準日經225指數今天早盤下跌3.3%或2235.93點，來到6萬5508.36點；韓國綜合股價指數（KOSPI）則重挫6%或363.73點，來到5645.08點。

彭博（Bloomberg）指出，記憶體大廠三星電子（Samsung Electronics）和SK海力士（SK Hynix）股價雙雙重挫6%以上；日本方面，IC載板廠Ibiden和記憶體廠鎧俠（Kioxia）等半導體相關類股跌幅居前。

隨著市場對利率走高、估值過高以及建構AI基礎設施龐大成本的疑慮升溫，美國一項備受關注的半導體類股指數已連跌6天，市值蒸發1.6兆美元（約新台幣51兆元）。即使三星和艾司摩爾（ASML）日前公布亮眼財報，也未能平息投資人的不安情緒。

美國昨晚公布最新數據顯示，9月消費者物價指數（CPI）漲幅高於市場預期，年增率升至3.7%，華爾街股市應聲收低，市場也押注聯準會（Fed）將更積極緊縮貨幣政策。

news.Title: 台股盤中暴跌逾1600點摔破47K 千家下殺僅3大族群紅盤
news.Content:
11:10更新：台股盤中跌幅擴大，一度重挫超過1600點摔破47K大關，觸及46995.24點跌幅逾3.4%，電子族群全面失守，僅食品、金融、汽車、觀光餐旅、造紙及資服類股紅盤苦撐。

美國通膨數據高於預期，升息機率上升，美日韓股接連下殺，日股跌逾3%，韓股也暴跌逾6%，台股今（15日）早盤以48382.75點開出，隨後下跌超過1400點觸及47193.41點，失守48K及月線，權值股面臨沉重賣壓，台積電跌70元觸及2420元，聯發科跌225元觸及42250元，台達電跌110元觸及1675元，鴻海跌4元觸及239元。電子股全面失守，僅金融股與內需族群較抗跌。

對此，摩爾投顧分析師林漢偉指出，市場對聯準會10月升息的預期快速升高，機率突破五成，壓抑科技成長股評價。加上AI相關融資傳出違約風險疑慮，半導體股遭到集中調節，費半重挫4.3%，四大指數尾盤跌勢進一步擴大。

台股面臨沉重下跌壓力，林漢偉認為，電子權值股面臨外資提款賣壓。台股指數恐再度失守月線，中小型股尤其要留意高本益比與前波漲多族群的補跌壓力。

美國通膨數據9月消費者物價指數（CPI）高於預期的年增率3.7%，使升息可能性上升，美股四大指數收黑，費城半導體指數暴跌4.30%，那斯達克指數挫低1.88%，標普500指數跌1.11%，台積電ADR下殺15.12美元（或3.40%）至430美元。

美國晶片股下殺，費城半導體指數晶片成分股的市值蒸發逾1兆美元，且費半指數在過去六個交易日累計下跌逾10%，可能創下2025年5月以來最長連續下跌的紀錄。主要受到高利率環境、估值過高及人工智慧基礎建設鉅額成本等因素影響。
