news.Title: Wall St futures drop as hot CPI revives Fed hike concerns; TSMC results in focus
news.Content:
Investing.com-- U.S. stock futures fell in Asian trading Thursday as investors assessed the prospect of further Federal Reserve tightening following hotter-than-expected inflation data, while weighing chipmaker TSMC's earnings for insights on AI-related demand.

S&P 500 Futures fell 0.4% to 7,740.25 points, while Nasdaq 100 Futures slid 1.1% to 29,842.75 points by 02:52 ET (06:52 GMT). Dow Jones Futures edged up 0.1% 51,913.0 points.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

The declines followed a broad sell-off on Wall Street, where technology and artificial intelligence-related shares came under pressure.

The NASDAQ Composite fell 1.9%, the S&P 500 lost 1.1%, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 0.1%.

The U.S. Labor Department reported that the Consumer Price Index rose 3.7% year-on-year in September, accelerating from 3.4% in August and exceeding economists' expectations for a 3.6% increase.

Core inflation, which excludes food and energy, climbed 2.6% annually, above forecasts for 2.5%, while monthly core prices increased 0.3%, against expectations for 0.2%.

Markets initially raised expectations of a rate increase at the Fed's October 27-28 meeting after the data, but those odds subsequently eased as Treasury yields retreated and policymakers signalled caution.

Comments from Fed officials, including Vice Chair Michelle Bowman and San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly, suggested policymakers could wait for a clearer picture of inflation before tightening policy further.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Investors were awaiting U.S. producer price and retail sales data, as well as remarks from Fed officials, for further clues on the policy outlook.

Investors were also assessing results from Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (TW:2330), the world's largest contract chipmaker and a key supplier to Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) and Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL).

The company reported a record third-quarter net profit of T$763.1 billion ($23.59 billion), up 69% from a year earlier and above estimates, as demand for AI processors continued to surge.

Its earnings outlook and commentary are closely watched for indications of whether strong AI infrastructure spending can sustain semiconductor growth.

Artificial intelligence-linked stocks were among the biggest losers on Wednesday. Data centre operator CoreWeave Inc (NASDAQ:CRWV) fell 16%, AI infrastructure company Nebius (NASDAQ:NBIS) dropped 11%, Oracle (NYSE:ORCL) declined 9%, and Dell Technologies (NYSE:DELL) slid 11%.

Story Continues

The sell-off reflected concerns about financing costs and elevated valuations after a strong rally in AI-related shares.

Markets are also monitoring developments in the Middle East, where the conflict involving Iran has pushed energy prices higher.

Oil prices fell 1.5% in Asian trading Thursday, with Brent holding near $104 per barrel.

news.Title: Tesla's Elon Musk Might Have Gone Back on His Word, but It's Working in China
news.Content: Rewind to 2019 when Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA) broke ground on its Giga Shanghai. Musk made it pretty clear at the time the factory was to produce more affordable versions of the Model 3 and Y for China. Sometime later, Tesla's CEO added, "Affordable cars must be made on same continent as customers." Things haven't quite gone according to plan thanks to China's domestic automakers rapidly developing their electric vehicle (EV) technology and a brutal price war that has forced all automakers to go back to the drawing board. Despite the change of plans, Tesla's exports from China ...
news.AI_Summary:
• Tesla's Giga Shanghai exports have surged, more than doubling to 361,972 vehicles in the first three quarters of 2026, nearly matching domestic sales.

• The bank views the order cuts as typical production adjustments rather than a sign of weaker demand, citing lead times that suggest strong demand for Pro models.
• Apple's split product launch, with the standard iPhone 18 delayed and a foldable iPhone Duo introduced, is expected to impact the December quarter's revenue.

news.Title: 美股平靜時光所剩不多 月底起四大事件接力、預期波動增50%
news.Content:
歷經波折不斷的夏季後，美股似乎進入一段平靜期。投資人或許該把握這段寧靜時光，因為選擇權市場正暗示本月下旬起，恐將迎來一波波動潮。

選擇權分析平台ORATS創辦人馬特·安伯森（Matt Amberson）向 MarketWatch 表示，當前情勢堪稱「暴風雨前的寧靜」。

根據道瓊市場數據（Dow Jones Market Data）分析選擇權定價結果，隨著美國聯準會（Fed）即將公布最新利率決策，自 10 月 28 日起標普 500 指數的預期單日波動幅度，平均將激增約 50%。

選擇權市場的定價顯示，隨著聯準會利率決策、重磅企業財報、美國期中選舉以及 10 月非農就業報告這「四大事件」自月底起接連登場，市場恐將告別平靜，並一舉觸發美股新一波劇烈波動。

其中最受矚目的重頭戲莫過於 11 月 3 日的期中選舉，而這波關鍵密集期將在 11 月 6 日公布的 10 月非農就業報告中畫下句點。

安伯森在電子郵件中表示，目前重大總體經濟催化因素不多，周三(14日)公布的消費者物價指數（CPI）報告是少數焦點。

不過，選擇權交易員正為本月底起更劇烈的行情預作準備，屆時投資人將接連面對聯準會決策、多家重要企業財報、期中選舉及 10 月就業報告。

類股輪動 壓低大盤波動

有華爾街「恐慌指數」之稱的芝加哥選擇權交易所波動率指數（VIX），數月來持續走低。然而，標普 500 成分股中仍有個股大幅震盪，不同產業股票的走勢也日益分歧。

這種檯面下的高度分化，有助於抑制指數層級的波動。當受惠人工智慧（AI）熱潮的股票表現疲弱時，所謂的「非 AI」股票便挺身支撐大盤，反之亦然。

BTIG 首席技術策略師克林斯基（Jonathan Krinsky）指出，截至週一為止，標普 500 指數已連續 52 個交易日未曾出現單日 1% 以上的跌幅。若再維持一天，這將創下 2020 年 1 月以來最長無顯著拉回紀錄。他認為，近期成交量萎縮無疑是造成大盤走勢沉悶的主因之一。

克林斯基在報告中分析，市場目前正處於重磅總經數據、關鍵催化劑與財報季之間的真空期，缺乏足以推動大盤的重大新消息，投資人普遍傾向觀望，靜待本週稍後大型銀行股開開首槍後再做決策。

他補充道，指數層級缺乏波動的時間長度，確實超出了他與許多市場人士的預期。

隨著美國大型銀行自周二起陸續公布業績，第三季財報季預料將正式進入高峰。

標普500距上次修正已久 超過歷史平均

標普 500 指數也已有一段時間未出現修正，通常定義為自近期高點下跌至少 10%。根據 Bespoke Investment Group 的分析，截至周一收盤，距離最近一次修正結束，已過了 552 個交易日。

H&R Block近期最明確的新變化，是管理層釋出高於市場預期的2027財年展望。公司預估營收為41.1億美元至41.6億美元，高於市場預估中值40.8億美元，調整後每股盈餘預估為6.04美元至6.24美元，也高於市場預期的5.86美元，顯示報稅與財務服務業務仍具韌性。

GameStop近期營運路線出現明顯轉向，正考慮撤回對eBay總額約560億美元的收購案，改為尋求合作夥伴關係或合資企業，主打交換卡與收藏品等高毛利品類。公司先前已把對eBay持股提高至9.75%，手中並握有84億美元現金，顯示其仍在尋找零售轉型以外的新成長載體。

This move is intended to accelerate joint development of next-generation X-ray-based process control solutions for semiconductor manufacturing. Onto Innovation will account for the stake at fair value option and will not consolidate Rigaku's results.

On the last earnings call, management highlighted that the estimates for the semiconductor X-ray technology market is approximately $1 billion at present, with increasingly complex 3D transistor and packaging technology expected to create additional opportunities.

Mapping the Competitive Terrain

news.Title: MKSI vs. ROK: Which Stock Is the Better Value Option?
news.Content:
Investors looking for stocks in the Electronics - Miscellaneous Products sector might want to consider either MKS (MKSI) or Rockwell Automation (ROK). But which of these two stocks is more attractive to value investors? We'll need to take a closer look to find out.

There are plenty of strategies for discovering value stocks, but we have found that pairing a strong Zacks Rank with an impressive grade in the Value category of our Style Scores system produces the best returns. The Zacks Rank favors stocks with strong earnings estimate revision trends, and our Style Scores highlight companies with specific traits.

MKS and Rockwell Automation are both sporting a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy) right now. This means that both companies have witnessed positive earnings estimate revisions, so investors should feel comfortable knowing that both of these stocks have an improving earnings outlook. However, value investors will care about much more than just this.

Value investors analyze a variety of traditional, tried-and-true metrics to help find companies that they believe are undervalued at their current share price levels.

The Value category of the Style Scores system identifies undervalued companies by looking at a number of key metrics. These include the long-favored P/E ratio, P/S ratio, earnings yield, cash flow per share, and a variety of other fundamentals that help us determine a company's fair value.

MKSI currently has a forward P/E ratio of 18.85, while ROK has a forward P/E of 28.90. We also note that MKSI has a PEG ratio of 0.52. This popular metric is similar to the widely-known P/E ratio, with the difference being that the PEG ratio also takes into account the company's expected earnings growth rate. ROK currently has a PEG ratio of 2.04.

Another notable valuation metric for MKSI is its P/B ratio of 5.6. Investors use the P/B ratio to look at a stock's market value versus its book value, which is defined as total assets minus total liabilities. By comparison, ROK has a P/B of 13.73.

Based on these metrics and many more, MKSI holds a Value grade of B, while ROK has a Value grade of D.

Both MKSI and ROK are impressive stocks with solid earnings outlooks, but based on these valuation figures, we feel that MKSI is the superior value option right now.

news.Title: 台股藏「誘多紅K」訊號！專家曝3招操作：別吃短線回檔的虧
news.Content:
台股今（14）日盤中一度逼近49,000點關卡，終場上漲284.52點，收在48,625.83點。資深分析師周代運對此提出警告，直言今日尾盤暗藏隱性賣壓，屬於極重的「誘多」紅K，呼籲投資人切勿急著追高滿倉，以免「吃短線回檔的虧」。他更提出三招操作策略，建議再等兩天打底。

周代運分析，全年台股長線目標上看53000點，且這波中期多頭趨勢、AI半導體產業週期與法人資金進場邏輯全部完好無損。不過，從今日盤面細節來看，雖然小漲284點，但「誘多屬性極重」，全天最大問題在於尾盤出現隱性出貨。盤中雖靠AI與半導體小幅拉抬穩住散戶信心，但在最後一小時，權值股與中大型電子股卻出現無聲賣壓，呈現緩緩倒貨、邊拉邊出的標準法人操作手法。

此外，今日反彈呈現「大跌有量、反彈無量」的縮量格局，屬於典型的「修復中繼盤」，代表買盤並未真正歸隊，只是空方暫時停手休息。周代運預估，盤面浮籌尚未洗乾淨、高檔獲利盤未充分消化，加上外部數據的不確定性，未來兩天將持續走區間震盪、來回洗盤、假突破真回踩的節奏。他強調，長線53000點是今年的終點價，但多頭行情永遠是「漲一段、洗一段、換籌碼、再創高」，現階段貿然追高不僅賺不到波段，還會因短線震盪洗盤而打亂心態與節奏。

周代運提出以下三招操作邏輯：

第一招：長線底倉，穩穩抱住，一股不賣。 中期53000點目標不變，產業趨勢與資金格局沒有破壞，手中低位布局的主流族群無須被短線洗盤洗掉籌碼。

第二招：短線活倉，全面停手、不追任何反彈。 未來兩天所有盤中拉高皆為短線減碼點而非加碼點，在尾盤賣壓未出清、量能未補、底部未夯實前，堅決不開新倉。

第三招：耐心等待二次回踩的低點機會 。這兩天透過震盪打底、小幅回檔測試支撐，才是最安全的低接窗口；待洗盤結束、籌碼乾淨且量能回溫後，再接回以迎接後續往53000點邁進的波段行情。

news.Title: History Says This Happens to Taiwan Semiconductor Stock After Oct. 15
news.Content:
Taiwan Semiconductor (NYSE: TSM) has a big day coming up on Oct. 15: its third-quarter earnings announcement. This is one of only four times in the year to receive an update on how one of the world's most important companies is doing, and Wall Street is expecting quite the quarter. However, Taiwan Semiconductor has a habit of exceeding expectations, which could ignite another rally in the stock.

So, what does history have to say about Taiwan Semiconductor's potential following earnings? Let's find out.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

An immediate reaction isn't always the case with Taiwan Semiconductor

The chart shows Taiwan Semiconductor's price action after earnings.

TSM data by YCharts.

As you can see, in three of the last four earnings reports, Taiwan Semiconductor's stock either declined or was weak following earnings. That's odd, considering it beat consensus earnings-per-share estimates, and it may be a telling sign of what's to come when it reports.

However, there's a longer-term picture here: Taiwan Semiconductor's stock has always done well about a month or two after reporting earnings. I think this just points to the overall trend in the artificial intelligence (AI) semiconductor industry , so even if TSMC's quarterly results fail to deliver a one-day price spike, there could still be substantial room to run.

The future looks bright for Taiwan Semiconductor

Taiwan Semiconductor is a logic chip manufacturer and makes chips for nearly every big tech company out there. Taiwan Semiconductor's size is unmatched, providing it with a competitive advantage over its peers. As a result of its connected status, it's a great heartbeat on the AI industry as a whole, and as AI spending ramps up, so will Taiwan Semiconductor's revenue growth.

For Q3, Wall Street analysts expect 47% revenue growth. For Q4, that figure climbs to 54%. Those would be the fastest rates TSMC has delivered over the past three years, which could make TSMC a great investment pick moving forward, as the market may not be ready for the growth it's expected to deliver.

TSM Revenue (Quarterly YoY Growth) data by YCharts.

Right now, TSMC is trading within its normal valuation range, at about 28 times forward earnings.

TSM PE Ratio (Forward) data by YCharts.

While that's "normal," TSMC is also expected to grow faster than normal, so this valuation may actually be cheap. One of TSMC's largest clients, Nvidia , noted that next year data center capital expenditures from the big five AI hyperscalers are expected to rise from nearly $800 billion in 2026 to $1.3 trillion in 2027. With TSMC supplying chips to nearly every computing unit maker, this should result in strong future growth for it. As a result, Taiwan Semiconductor could be well-positioned to deliver strong end-of-year gains following its Q3 earnings report. While history doesn't support a one-day spike following earnings, a strong couple of months to close out the year could be in the cards.

Story Continues

Taiwan Semiconductor also has another catalyst in hand -- the company is raising foundry prices by 5% to 10% starting in 2027. While that won't help its third-quarter earnings, the price increase will add to TSMC's already impressive bottom line next year, particularly as its clients have nowhere else to go given TSMC's immense scale.

So, whether Taiwan Semiconductor's stock rallies immediately after earnings or a few months later, I think the long-term outlook for the stock is clear: Taiwan Semiconductor is a great buy today due to its leadership in chip fabrication. Without Taiwan Semiconductor, AI wouldn't look the same, and its status makes it a must-own stock.

news.Title: AI Memory Chip Selloff Looks Overblown: 2 Stocks to Buy on the Dip
news.Content:
Memory stocks are facing fresh selling pressure since Monday as investors question the sustainability of artificial intelligence (AI)-related spending and worry about rising competition. The latest trigger came from China's ChangXin Memory Technologies, which reported progress over the weekend on a new DRAM architecture that it claims could boost memory density by 30-50%, allowing more data to be stored in the same physical space.

The market reaction has been sharp. Per CNBC, SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics dropped more than 10% and 7%, respectively, yesterday in Seoul. Both touched their lowest levels since August.

In the United States, Micron Technology MU, Sandisk Corporation SNDK, Seagate Technology Holdings STX and Western Digital Corporation WDC have also come under pressure. Over the past two trading sessions, shares of Micron, Sandisk, Seagate and Western Digital fell 4.4%, 6.2%, 4.5% and 4.1%, respectively, reflecting growing nervousness across the memory sector. Investors were already worried about how AI spending is being financed, so the CXMT news landed on a fragile market.

However, the sell-off may be getting ahead of itself. Although CXMT's technological progress could intensify competition over time, the company still needs to prove that it can manufacture its chips at scale. Legacy memory makers still hold a technological lead over CXMT.

For investors, this pullback could present an opportunity rather than a reason to panic. Micron and Sandisk are worth buying now on the recent dip, as both are set to benefit from continued demand for memory and storage driven by AI infrastructure.

Let's assess why these two stocks still offer attractive opportunities despite the recent volatility.

Micron

Micron closed fiscal 2026 on a strong note, with record revenues, high margins and strong cash generation. The outlook is even more striking. The company expects fiscal first-quarter 2027 revenues of $61.5 billion (plus or minus $1.5 billion) and adjusted earnings of $38.15 per share (plus or minus $1), implying roughly 351% revenue growth and 698% earnings growth from a year ago.

HBM revenues grew faster than Micron's total revenues in the fiscal fourth quarter, and the company has already contracted most of its 2027 HBM supply at significantly higher prices. Its HBM4 ramp is progressing, and it is working with NVIDIA on a custom HBM4E solution. NAND is a second engine, with data center SSD revenues approaching $10 billion in the fiscal fourth quarter, more than 10 times the year-earlier level, as uses like KV-cache offload widen demand for fast storage. Further out, autonomous vehicles and humanoid robots should need far more memory and storage than today's devices.

Story Continues

Micron is also trying to make this boom more durable. It has signed 26 Strategic Customer Agreements, which are expected to account for more than 35% of revenues through 2030. Customer financial commitments have risen to $32 billion, mostly as cash deposits. That could soften the industry's usual boom-and-bust swings. New capacity is coming from the United States, Singapore, Japan and Taiwan, with Singapore HBM packaging due to start in early 2027 and the ID1 fab in mid-2027. Risks remain, including heavy capital spending and slower price increases, but fundamentals suggest that the long-term story is intact.

MU currently sports a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) and has a VGM Score of A.

Micron Technology, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Micron Technology, Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Micron Technology, Inc. Quote

Sandisk

Sandisk has become one of the biggest winners of the AI memory boom, and since its separation from Western Digital it offers a more direct way to invest in demand for NAND flash and data storage. The reason lies in how AI is changing storage needs. As inference and agentic AI generate more data that must be stored, retrieved and served with low delay, NAND is becoming central to architectures built around KV cache and RAG. Sandisk is scaling its datacenter business accordingly, widening its enterprise SSD range and moving toward QLC products. It now expects 2026 datacenter exabyte growth in the mid-70% range. It believes demand keeps rising on a rolling basis, and sees the enterprise datacenter flash market reaching about 1.2 zettabytes by 2030.

What sets Sandisk apart is its effort to escape NAND's usual swings in spot prices. Its eight New Business Model agreements are expected to cover more than half of its bits in fiscal 2027 and roughly two-thirds in fiscal 2028. At floor pricing, the signed deals represent at least $93.9 billion in revenues.

For fiscal first-quarter 2027, Sandisk expects revenues of $10.3 billion to $10.8 billion, up from $8.97 billion recorded in the last reported quarter. With multi-year agreements providing visibility and AI inference driving storage demand, the company looks well placed for the years ahead.

SNDK currently sports a Zacks Rank #1 and has a VGM Score of A.

news.Title: Cisco (CSCO): Can Its Earnings Recovery Turn Into Lasting Cash Growth?
news.Content:
Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ: CSCO ) has an opportunity to turn artificial-intelligence infrastructure spending and network upgrades into stronger cash generation. Fiscal-2026 net income increased 30% to $13.3 billion, but operating cash flow stayed near $14.2 billion. Reported earnings also benefited from higher unrealized investment gains, which increased profit without generating operating cash. Cisco's cybersecurity business adds another growth avenue as companies strengthen their defenses against evolving threats. Find our rankings of cybersecurity stocks here.

Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) trades at approximately 20x forward earnings and 32x trailing earnings. The earnings outlook combines operating growth with accounting exclusions. Fiscal-2027 guidance calls for GAAP EPS of $4.00–$4.06, against $3.33 in fiscal 2026, and company-defined non-GAAP adjusted EPS of $5.05–$5.11. Adjustments include stock compensation, acquisition-related amortization, and restructuring. The lower forward multiple should not be read as pure profit growth.

Arista Networks, Inc. (NYSE:ANET) is the closest operating comparison because it competes in network switching. Its 45.4% second-quarter GAAP operating margin sets a high profitability benchmark for Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO). Hewlett Packard Enterprise Company (NYSE:HPE) has greater server exposure, and its inventory commitments create a different cash-conversion test . The 20x forward valuation looks reasonable only if its fourth-quarter cash rebound persists.

Installed Networks Support Growth, but Require Funding

Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) benefits from established enterprise networks, customer relationships, and the cost of replacing integrated equipment and software. Management says more than half its customers purchase both campus and data-center networking. That breadth creates opportunities to sell upgrades into existing relationships and spread development and support expenses across more revenue. Billionaire Ken Fisher also holds a position in Cisco, reflecting investor interest in the networking company. See which other AI stocks are on the billionaire's radar.

AI demand strengthens that opportunity. Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) booked $9.3 billion in hyperscaler AI infrastructure orders in fiscal 2026 and recognized about $4 billion in associated revenue. Management expects $7.5 billion of AI infrastructure revenue in fiscal 2027. The difference between bookings and sales matters because large AI orders can arrive well before shareholder cash .

Story Continues

Revenue guidance of $72.2 billion–$73.4 billion implies approximately 15% growth at the midpoint. The adjusted EPS midpoint implies about 17% growth from fiscal-2026 adjusted EPS of $4.33. Those forecasts require operating leverage as shipments increase, while memory shortages and higher component prices can absorb part of the benefit.

Subscription revenue gives Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) a recurring base, but it increased only about 1% to $32.0 billion in fiscal 2026. Maintaining that base supports investment; it does not yet establish accelerating software cash growth. Hardware expansion still requires inventory purchases before customer payments arrive, and competitive pricing can limit the profit retained from additional shipments.

A Better Quarter Has Not Removed the Cash Burden

Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) generated $5.4 billion of fourth-quarter operating cash flow, up 27%. That is meaningful evidence against treating the annual cash plateau as permanent. Fiscal 2026 also included the final $2.3 billion U.S. transition-tax payment, removing one specific future cash obligation.

Working capital nevertheless remains demanding. Annual inventory and financing-receivable movements absorbed approximately $2.5 billion and $1.8 billion, respectively. Both continued consuming cash in the fourth quarter, when their combined use approached $2.8 billion. Higher deferred revenue and other liabilities helped offset those demands. The rebound did not come from releasing inventory or collecting down customer financing.

Offering payment flexibility can support equipment sales, but customer financing earns its keep only when collections justify the risk . Persistently larger financing balances would tie up capital and reduce the cash available for distributions, even if reported sales and earnings continued growing.

Non-GAAP free cash flow, defined as operating cash flow less purchases of property and equipment, declined 4% to $12.8 billion as capital spending increased. Dividends and buybacks consumed approximately 99% of that amount. Sustaining distributions alongside growth investment therefore depends on better conversion, not simply higher accounting profit.

Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) produced $13.3 billion of free cash flow in fiscal 2025 before the latest decline. The business has demonstrated substantial cash generation, but stronger AI demand now brings heavier funding requirements. At 20x forward earnings, shareholders need growth that increases cash after those commitments. More sales alone would provide little valuation protection if funding needs absorbed the additional profit.

Conclusion

Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) looks reasonably valued at 20x forward earnings if the fourth-quarter cash recovery becomes sustained growth. Installed relationships and stronger infrastructure demand make that outcome credible. It requires earnings growth to produce more cash after investment, with inventory and financing needs growing more slowly than sales. Continued working-capital expansion alongside flat free cash flow would make the valuation demanding, even if orders remained strong.

While we acknowledge the potential of CSCO as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. If you're looking for an extremely undervalued AI stock that also stands to benefit significantly from Trump-era tariffs and the onshoring trend, see our free report on the best short-term AI stock .

news.Title: Lumentum Is Sold Out Through 2029. Could Tower Semiconductor Be the Next Big Winner?
news.Content:
Lumentum (LITE) is apparently having a problem that most companies would love to have: More demand for its products than it can accommodate.

According to a Seeking Alpha report, Lumentum CEO Michael Hurlston recently said the company's components are sold out through 2029. Wedbush Securities believes that could be bullish news for suppliers and semiconductor foundries.

More News from Barchart

Why It's Time to Load Up on Marvell Stock

Dear Accenture Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for Oct. 14

Dear Nvidia Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for October 13

Tired of missing midday reversals? The FREE Barchart Brief newsletter keeps you in the know. Sign up now!

One company that could benefit is Tower Semiconductor (TSEM), an Israeli chipmaker that's building a growing business around the technology that connects artificial intelligence data centers.

About Tower Semiconductor Stock

Tower operates semiconductor foundries—factories that manufacture specialized chips designed by other companies. Its products serve industries ranging from automotive and telecommunications to medical equipment and aerospace.

But one of its most interesting opportunities lies in silicon photonics, a technology that uses light rather than electrical signals to transmit information. That's increasingly important for AI data centers, where thousands of processors must communicate at tremendous speeds. Traditional electrical connections can consume substantial power and face limitations as data distance and volume increase.

Optical connections can move information quickly over longer distances while reducing some of those power demands. And Tower manufactures the specialized components that help make those connections possible.

Shares of TSEM have been through the roof, jumping nearly 200% in the last year, pushing the company's market cap to $23.7 billion.

Tower Is Already Seeing Increased Demand

Tower isn't simply waiting for the optical communications market to take off.

In May, the company announced $1.3 billion in silicon photonics contracts for 2027, along with $290 million in customer prepayments to reserve manufacturing capacity. It also reported larger contractual wafer commitments for 2028.

Then, in September, Tower and NewPhotonics announced high-volume shipments of optical chips supporting data transmission speeds of 800 gigabits to 1.6 terabits per second.

And on Tuesday, Tower announced an expanded multiyear agreement with Semtech (SMTC), which is reserving additional manufacturing capacity for components used in AI data center connections.

Story Continues

Those developments suggest that customers are committing to Tower's manufacturing technology. Its quarterly earnings just reinforce that narrative. Revenue in the second quarter was $460 million, up 24% from a year ago to set a quarterly company record. Net profit excluding nonrecurring items was also a record, coming in at $91 million, up 95% from the previous year.

"We began the year stating that Tower will have a very strong second half as the previously announced capacity investments become qualified and converted into shipments," CEO Russell Ellwanger told analysts in the company's earnings call. "Beginning the second half of 2026 with a $2 billion run rate turns the page into multiple new exciting chapters for the company. The strength of our customer demand, our growing partnerships, our proven execution capabilities, and the strategic investments that we have and still continue to announce provide a powerful catalyst to accelerate our short, mid- and long-term growth."

Tower has scheduled its third-quarter report for Nov. 2. Management expects revenue of between $494 million and $526 million, which would be an increase of 31% at the midpoint.

What Do Analysts Expect From TSEM Stock?

Tower is slowly getting attention from Wall Street analysts—only four analysts surveyed by Barchart covered TSEM stock just three months ago, but that number has nearly doubled. And the group has a consensus "Strong Buy" recommendation, with a mean price target of $309.89 that suggests a potential upside of 48%.

Lumentum's capacity commitments don't guarantee additional business for Tower. The company still needs to expand production, meet customer requirements, and turn manufacturing commitments into delivered products.

But there's an important distinction here. Tower isn't relying entirely on predictions about future AI demand. It already has substantial customer commitments and optical components moving into high-volume production.

As AI data centers grow, the connections between processors are becoming increasingly significant. Tower offers investors exposure to that opportunity without having to compete directly in the market for advanced AI processors.

That's a business worth paying attention to.

news.Title: AWS Backlog Hits $496 Billion While Cloud Margins Surge to 39% Making Amazon a Must-Own Growth Stock
news.Content:
Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) has become one of the most compelling buys among Magnificent Seven stocks and large-cap growth stocks in general. There are two converging factors that make Amazon a screaming buy right now.

One is surging growth, supported by a massive $496 billion Amazon Web Services cloud computing backlog , which is contracts in the pipeline waiting to be executed upon. That is up more than double from the start of 2026 when it had just $244 billion in backlog.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

That should allow Amazon to continue the momentum it has seen so far this year. The fiscal second quarter was Amazon's best quarter in more than four years. Overall revenue increased 20% to $200.6 billion, marking its best quarter of revenue growth since 2021.

Operating margin rises 650 basis points

Amazon's cash cow, its AWS business, saw sales jump 37%, marking its best results in 18 quarters. In addition, Amazon saw its AWS operating margin jump 650 basis points to 39.4%, up from 32.9% in Q2 2025. If you exclude a one-time accounting gain, its a 520 basis point increase.

Overall, net income rose to $62.6 billion Q2, or $5.75 per share, up from $1.68 per share in Q2 2025. That is skewed by a huge $53.4 billion gain from its investment in Anthropic, but it still beat adjusted earnings estimates. That is significant growth, especially in the face of huge capital expenditures, which had concerned a lot of investors earlier this year, thinking it would crush earnings.

That leads to the second major factor that makes Amazon a buy: its valuation.

Too cheap to ignore

Amazon stock started the year trending lower out of concerns about its then $200 billion proposed for capital expenditures, now $220 billion. Investors were worried earlier this year for a few reasons -- one, the number was 50% higher than 2025; two, its AWS cloud business saw slowing growth and was losing market share; and three, it would eat into their free cash flow and lead to negative cash flow in Q2.

The stock price has since recovered and is now up about 13% year-to-date. As noted, the concerns about overspending on capex were somewhat alleviated by surging growth, an overflowing pipeline, and the realization that the spending is needed to meet demand.

Cash flow was negative in Q2, but CEO Andy Jassy said on the recent earnings call that "when demand is necessitating so many data centers being built simultaneously in advance of when we can start monetizing them, we'll spend a lot of capex and encounter free cash flow headwinds until these data centers come online." But after a few years when the servers are being used, revenue growth will outpace capex growth and free cash flow will return -- at least that's the plan.

Story Continues

Despite these cash flow headwinds, Amazon looks like a must own stock right now for not just its growth, but its cheap valuation. It is trading at around 20 times earnings, which is near the lowest it has been in more than 10 years. It is a compelling buy at this valuation, given its overflowing near half a trillion dollar pipeline.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger

Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005.

But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout, a massive technology build-out that Google's CEO says could be more profound than fire or electricity.

While everyone watches the chip designers, one "backbone" company provides the critical technology that Nvidia and AMD literally cannot function without. We've detailed this under-the-radar player in our new AI Playbook.

news.Title: Michael Burry Questions Microsoft’s AI Spending. Is Its Valuation Misleading?
news.Content:
Michael Burry has questioned whether Microsoft's AI spending is driven by necessity, suggesting the company may be using its financial figures as leverage, according to Seeking Alpha. He argues Big Tech is spending wildly because it assumes it will be granted an oligopoly too big to fail. Michael Burry reportedly owns Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ: MSFT ) shares and long-dated call options, so this is skepticism about spending, not a short thesis.

Separately, the company made an accounting change at the start of fiscal 2027: it now assumes its data centers and office buildings last 25 years instead of 15. It's worth examining because it changes how that spending is reported. Microsoft's AI spending is under scrutiny, but its cybersecurity business offers another investment angle. See where it stands in our list of the 10 Best Cybersecurity Stocks to Buy According to Analysts .

Why I Think Burry Has a Point

Microsoft counts finance leases in its capex but leaves out operating leases. One key test for a finance lease is whether it covers most of a building's useful life. With buildings now expected to last 25 years, more leases fall short of that bar and become operating leases. As a result, Microsoft's calendar 2026 capex forecast dropped from about $190 billion to about $175 billion. CFO Amy Hood said that outside of this change, the company's spending plans were unchanged. So the $15 billion drop came from accounting. Microsoft has also signed a huge number of new data center leases. Leases that haven't started yet jumped from $196.6 billion to $329.1 billion in just one quarter. Under the revised lease classifications, more future data center leases will be treated as operating leases rather than included in Microsoft's reported capex. With the company's future data center commitments rising despite a lower capex forecast, investors may want to see which other growth stocks billionaires are backing , including MSFT.

The Valuation Isn't Quite What It Seems

On paper, Microsoft looks reasonably priced. The forward non-GAAP P/E of 26.80x sits about 12% below its 5-year average of 30.51x. Analysts expect EPS to grow 14% this fiscal year, then about 20% and 22% over the next two. The same accounting change also affects earnings. The issue is that the same accounting change affects both earnings and how spending is reported. For a new building, stretching its assumed life from 15 to 25 years cuts yearly depreciation by about 40%. Microsoft says the boost to fiscal 2027 operating income will be minimal, but as more buildings come online, earnings will look better than they would have under the old rules. Meanwhile, the $329.1 billion in leases yet to begin won't appear on the balance sheet until they start, so investors have to track them separately. So earnings could look stronger, and obligations smaller, than they really are. That's why I don't think the stock is quite as cheap as its P/E makes it look.

Story Continues

Hedge fund interest cooled slightly. Funds holding Microsoft fell from 282 in Q1 to 273 in Q2. The value of their stakes, though, rose from $63.6 billion to $66.5 billion.

Microsoft did disclose this change on its earnings call. Still, Burry is right that the headline capex number no longer tells the full story, and Microsoft's valuation may be more demanding than its reported earnings multiple suggests. I'd track total lease commitments alongside capex to see what Microsoft is really spending,

While we acknowledge the potential of MSFT as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. news.Title: PAYX Shares Rise 17.7% in Six Months: Here's What You Should Know
news.Content:
Paychex PAYX stock has gained 17.7% over the past six months compared with the industry's 22.9% growth. The Zacks S&P 500 Composite gained 10.7% during the same period.

Six-Month Share Price Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Let us delve deeper into the factors contributing to the company's strong performance.

AI-Driven Innovation to Boost Growth & Margins

Paychex is leveraging artificial intelligence (AI) to expand its offerings, enhance service delivery and improve efficiency. Its WISE platform uses more than 50 trillion proprietary data points to streamline payroll and HR workflows. In a pilot covering more than 50,000 businesses, WISE helped prevent approximately 90% of targeted payroll errors. The company has deployed more than 2,000 AI agents and features, increasing automated payroll processing by nearly 20% from January through August 2026. New offerings such as WISE Hire and WISE Pro drive revenue growth, while greater automation supports productivity and margin expansion.

Paycor Integration Boosts PAYX Cross-Selling Opportunities

The Paycor acquisition has expanded Paychex's enterprise reach and cross-selling opportunities across HR, benefits and advisory solutions. Its One Paychex strategy supports broader product adoption and higher customer value. In first-quarter fiscal 2027, enterprise bookings grew at a double-digit rate, while broker referrals rose 43% year over year. The rollout of Paychex Perks to approximately 2.5 million Paycor employees further expands cross-selling potential. Continued revenue synergies, wider distribution and improving sales productivity support long-term growth.

PAYX's Recurring Revenues & Cost Discipline Support Margins

Paychex's recurring revenue model, improving client retention and pricing power underpin its earnings growth. In first-quarter fiscal 2027, revenues rose 6% to $1.6 billion, while adjusted EPS increased 10% to $1.34. Adjusted operating margin expanded 130 basis points to 42%, aided by productivity gains and cost discipline. Management reaffirmed its fiscal 2027 revenue growth outlook of 5-6% and adjusted operating margin target of approximately 44%. Continued pricing gains, higher product penetration and AI-driven efficiencies should support sustained profitability and earnings growth.

PAYX's Cash Generation Supports Shareholder Returns

Paychex's consistent cash generation supports dividends and disciplined capital allocation. In fiscal 2026, operating cash flow reached $2.6 billion and free cash flow totaled $2.3 billion, with $2.2 billion returned to shareholders. In first-quarter fiscal 2027, the company paid $424.1 million in dividends, while operating cash flow reached $413.5 million despite tax payment timing effects. Continued earnings growth and prudent capital deployment should sustain long-term shareholder returns.

news.Title: 股價區間曝光！ 台積電法說會倒數引爆對決 多空豪賭2.57兆元行情
news.Content:
晶圓代工龍頭台積電15日將舉行法說會，成為股價下一步走勢的重要觀察點。儘管第3季營收已優於財測，市場利多提前反映，投資人接下來更關注毛利率、第4季營運展望，以及AI需求能否支撐目前的高估值。外媒報導，選擇權市場預期台積電財報公布後股價可能波動約4%，以公司約2.1兆美元市值計算，牽動的市值可能超過800億美元（約新台幣2.57兆元）。

台積電ADR周二收在445.12美元，較10月初高點下跌約9%。儘管股價回檔，選擇權市場仍預期財報公布後可能出現明顯反應，顯示市場正等待新的營運訊號。

選擇權預告股價波動4％ 毛利率成財報焦點

據財經媒體《Invezz》報導，10月16日到期的選擇權顯示，台積電財報公布後的預期股價波動幅度約為4%。截至周二收盤，履約價445美元的買權與賣權合計約18美元，對應的股價區間約為427至463美元。

市場部位也集中在接近現價的履約價。450美元買權未平倉合約超過9500口，440美元賣權則超過6000口，這些價位可作為觀察財報後短期股價反應的參考。

由於第3季營收數字已經揭曉，利潤率將是市場檢視的重點。台積電第3季營收達新台幣1.49兆元，約467億美元，年增50%，高於原先446億至458億美元的財測。

不過，台積電先前預估第3季毛利率為65%至67%，營業利益率為56%至58%，均低於第2季的67.7%與60.3%。市場將關注實際表現是否符合預期，以及獲利能力能否支撐股價。

分析師看好獲利成長 第4季財測更受關注

倫敦證券交易所集團（LSEG）的SmartEstimate預測，台積電第3季淨利將年增65%，達新台幣7463億元，有望連續第6季創下獲利紀錄。

美國銀行分析師Haas Liu預期，第3季毛利率將接近67%，第4季營收則可望季增10%至15%。他也將台積電ADR目標價由590美元上調至620美元，並認為以2027年預估獲利計算，約16倍的本益比並不高。

相較於單季獲利，第4季展望可能更直接影響市場對台積電後續成長的評價。摩根士丹利分析師預期，台積電可能將2026年營收成長預測，由目前的超過40%上調至400%出頭至400%中段的區間。法說會對未來營收成長的說明，將成為投資人判斷股價能否獲得進一步支撐的關鍵。

AI需求與資本支出 左右台積電估值能否維持

除了財報數字，台積電能否持續受惠於AI需求，同時控制先進製程與海外擴廠成本，也是市場關注的焦點。

台積電今年7月將2026年資本支出預測上調至600億至640億美元。美國銀行分析師Haas Liu預估，今年支出約630億美元，2027年可能高達830億美元，主要用於擴充3奈米、2奈米、A16製程及先進封裝產能。

投資人將關注輝達與客製化AI加速器需求、CoWoS先進封裝產能，以及2奈米製程進度。由於新製程成本較高，在產能利用率提升前，可能對毛利率形成壓力。

因此，這場法說會不只是檢視台積電第3季是否再創獲利紀錄，更重要的是公司能否提出足以支撐未來成長的展望。若毛利率與第4季營運指引優於市場預期，將有助

news.Title: 曾文生：科技業資金投入電力建設 台電碳捕捉計畫不缺席
news.Content:
電廠或電網投資金額巨大，近日討論讓民間科技業如台積電等出錢參與議題興起，台電也有相關規劃。台電董事長曾文生14日指出，近期已有報導台積電正跟民營電力公司研商碳捕捉與封存(CCS)，而台電身為國營事業，自然不會缺席。他透露目前已有廠商來接洽，可相關工作還要共同規劃跟決策。

曾文生直指台電這家電力公司長期走向，就是要「產業化」，未來要與產業共同決策，這已經開始在做了。做伺服器、封裝、記憶體、晶圓製造的產業，從園區的開發開始，到規劃用電，雙方都需要共同規劃出一個機制，這慢慢正在開始。

他說近日已經有媒體披露，台積電正跟民營電力公司共同研商碳捕捉與封存(CCS)相關工作，台電身為國營事業，雖然研議階段不能說，但這件事情不會缺席。

台電有11座火力電廠，先前就規劃在台中火力電廠設置「減碳技術示範園區」，於9號機設置碳捕捉（CCUS）裝置，預計明年底正式啟用，每年可捕捉2000公噸二氧化碳。

只是，與民間合作在電廠做CCS，哪些人要來做，產能規劃多少，後端要怎麼加裝輔助裝置，以及碳捕捉下來是要再利用還是封存？曾文生指需要與業界共同規劃跟決策。他透露已有需求者來找台電，但是還不能講(哪家企業)。

至於科技業為何願意出錢投資電力建設？曾文生回應，當年Apple是拿著錢來台灣包產能，現在很多半導體的製造者，也拿一些資金去支持一些獨角獸、不錯的供應商，讓他們去擴張產能。

雖然與科技業共同投資決策已經是方向，可是他強調，現在還不能說達成了一個什麼共識，雙方怎麼做，需要彼此有一些討論的時間空間。

news.Title: 台股暴漲暴跌是空頭？郭哲榮曝真相：台積電法說有驚喜
news.Content:
台股今（14）日行情如驚濤駭浪，加權指數早盤一度猛攻超過 700 點、逼近 49,000 點大關，終場大漲 284.52 點，收在 48,625.83 點，成交金額達 9,286.24 億元。前一日盤中暴跌近千點，今日又上演劇烈洗盤震盪，讓不少散戶驚慌失措，質疑台股暴漲暴跌是否為空頭訊號？ 摩爾投顧投資長郭哲榮 特別指出，這絕非空頭來臨，而是主力洗盤甩轎的極限過程，大跌反而是上天給予樂觀者的絕佳禮物，並搶先預告台積電(2330)法說會的震撼財測，為市場注入強心針。

【暴漲暴跌是空頭訊號嗎？郭哲榮曝關鍵內幕】

面對台股近期的大幅波動，許多投資人焦慮難眠，郭哲榮分析指出，今日台股開高後尾盤漲幅收斂，主因是受到韓國股市重挫拖累，並非台股基本面轉壞。 這波暴漲暴跌實為主力清洗浮動籌碼的甩轎手段，絕非空頭架構。

他更首度透露關鍵內幕，表示自己在大盤重挫近千點時完全沒有恐慌拋售，反而選擇逆向操作、密集加碼優質個股。他感性地分享獨門投資哲學：「悲觀的人邏輯正確，樂觀的人賺大錢！」提醒投資人切勿在市場最絕望時跟風殺低，唯有保持理性與信心，才能在危機中把握財富重組的良機。

【揭密獨門投資心法 散戶翻身看兩大指引】

談到散戶長期無法獲利的痛點，郭哲榮直言，許多散戶同時持有十檔以上的股票，資金過於分散反而大幅增加風險， 正確做法是精簡持股、集中資金才能直球對決。

對於總經與權值股風向，他提出兩大關鍵指引：

1. 美CPI數據與降息預期： 市場預估美國CPI通膨數據達3.6%已被充分消化，10月聯準會不升息機率高達79%，一旦利空出盡，將直接帶動台股與AI族群迎來新一波行情。

2. 預測台積電法說會震撼彈： 在台積電(2330)法說會前夕，郭哲榮搶先預估其第四季營收將達 525 億至 530 億美元，季增高達 12% 以上，全年營收成長更將衝破 43% 至 45%，遠優於市場預期。

【逆風中的曙光！低基期與被動元件迎契機】

在洗盤後的黑夜裡，潛力標的已展露曙光。郭哲榮點出，被動元件族群如國巨(2327)（指出逢600元以下為買點）、華新科(2492)與日電貿(3090)等已展現築底回溫的強勁態勢；而精材(3374)、智原(3035)、華邦電(2344)與南亞科(2408)等低基期股票，更是具備爆發力的精選標的。

郭哲榮感性結語，投資是一場克服恐慌的心理戰，只要看清AI產業大趨勢、選對低基期優質個股，隨同年底前AI族群回溫的浪潮，定能在這波震撼洗盤過後迎來豐收。

news.Title: 施羅德首檔主動式ETF 00419A於11/2開募 10元甜甜價搶搭台股AI浪潮
news.Content:
全球資產管理巨頭施羅德投信今（14）日宣布，正式將主動式ETF版圖延伸至台灣，推出深耕台灣近40年來的首檔主動式ETF「施羅德AI科技台股主動式ETF」 (00419A-TW) 。該基金預計於 11 月 2 日至 11 月 6 日進行募集，發行價格為新台幣 10 元，最低申購門檻僅需 1 萬元，並採季配息（預定 3/6/9/12 月）且導入收益平準金機制，滿足投資人追求資本利得與現金流的需求。

截至 2026 年 8 月底，施羅德在台管理資產規模已達新台幣 5,673 億元。施羅德投信董事長謝誠晃表示：「台灣不僅是全球科技產業重鎮，也是亞洲最活躍、發展最迅速的ETF市場之一。ETF架構兼具靈活性與高透明度，而主動式管理能讓我們適時因應市場變化、發掘潛在的新興贏家，建構高信心的投資組合。」

施羅德全球ETF主管 Tom Stephen 亦指出，台灣企業處於半導體創新與下一代科技發展的最前線，隨著AI應用加速滲透，產業鏈蘊含極大的投資潛力。本次結合施羅德全球橫跨 24 個地區、逾 650 位專業投資人的研究平台，將發揮深厚的台股選股實力。

針對投資人最關心的選股策略，施羅德台股團隊00419A基金經理人游信凱於記者會上直言，這一波AI浪潮與過去產業景氣循環不同，而是「產品規格升級帶來的選擇性成長週期」。隨著雲端服務商（CSP）資本支出持續激增，預估明年資本支出將突破 1.06 兆美元，AI 算力對於基礎建設的要求已不可同日而語。

游信凱進一步分析，當前單一晶片功耗大幅提升，一架AI伺服器機櫃的功耗動輒高達 125 千瓦（kW），「這相當於一棟大樓的用電量在持續運轉！」因此，龐大的發熱與耗電需求，將帶動電源供應、散熱模組（如液冷技術）、電力基礎建設與重電族群的強勁規格升級需求。

00419A 將從超過 300 檔AI相關企業中，精選出 30 檔以上的優質個股，三大核心佈局方向包含：

關鍵零組件與半導體：包含先進製程、先進封裝（CoWoS）、IC設計與高速傳輸。

基礎建設與電力散熱：涵蓋散熱模組、重電設備與不斷電系統等算力支援供應鏈。

新型AI應用與軟硬整合：延伸至邊緣AI、機器人開發及新軟體應用等未來十年的潛力領域。

面對市場關注主動式ETF如何擊敗大盤，施羅德團隊強調，台股科技產業並非所有公司都能吃到訂單，唯有能夠滿足科技大廠嚴格規格要求的企業才能脫穎而出。團隊每天透過嚴謹的基本面分析與評判，尋找具備產品升級能力與獲利上修潛力的個股。

游信凱指出：「我們追求的是長期績效表現與高信念的投資佈局，而非短線跟風。透過團隊合作與徹底的基本面功課，協助投資人不僅能喝到AI浪潮的『肉湯』，更能精準抓到最核心的獲利主軸。」

施羅德AI科技台股主動式ETF (00419A) 將於 11 月 2 日正式募集，風險報酬等級為 RR5，提供投資人以小額資金靈活卡位全球AI供應鏈核心的絕佳工具。

During this period, the Zacks Computer - Integrated Systems industry, which Silicon Motion falls in, has gained 3.9%. The key question now is: What could be the stock's future direction?

Although media reports or rumors about a significant change in a company's business prospects usually cause its stock to trend and lead to an immediate price change, there are always certain fundamental factors that ultimately drive the buy-and-hold decision.

Revisions to Earnings Estimates

Rather than focusing on anything else, we at Zacks prioritize evaluating the change in a company's earnings projection. This is because we believe the fair value for its stock is determined by the present value of its future stream of earnings.

Our analysis is essentially based on how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to take the latest business trends into account. When earnings estimates for a company go up, the fair value for its stock goes up as well. And when a stock's fair value is higher than its current market price, investors tend to buy the stock, resulting in its price moving upward. Because of this, empirical studies indicate a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and short-term stock price movements.

Silicon Motion is expected to post earnings of $3.30 per share for the current quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +230%. Over the last 30 days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate remained unchanged.

For the current fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $11.16 points to a change of +214.4% from the prior year. Over the last 30 days, this estimate has remained unchanged.

For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $16.34 indicates a change of +46.5% from what Silicon Motion is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has remained unchanged.

With an impressive externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool -- the Zacks Rank -- is a more conclusive indicator of a stock's near-term price performance, as it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. The size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, has resulted in a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) for Silicon Motion.

Story Continues

The chart below shows the evolution of the company's forward 12-month consensus EPS estimate:

12 Month EPS

Revenue Growth Forecast

Even though a company's earnings growth is arguably the best indicator of its financial health, nothing much happens if it cannot raise its revenues. It's almost impossible for a company to grow its earnings without growing its revenue for long periods. Therefore, knowing a company's potential revenue growth is crucial.

For Silicon Motion, the consensus sales estimate for the current quarter of $532.81 million indicates a year-over-year change of +120.2%. For the current and next fiscal years, $1.89 billion and $2.51 billion estimates indicate +112.9% and +33.3% changes, respectively.

Last Reported Results and Surprise History

Silicon Motion reported revenues of $451 million in the last reported quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +127%. EPS of $2.43 for the same period compares with $0.69 a year ago.

Compared to the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $403.64 million, the reported revenues represent a surprise of +11.73%. The EPS surprise was +14.08%.

Over the last four quarters, Silicon Motion surpassed consensus EPS estimates three times. The company topped consensus revenue estimates each time over this period.

Valuation

No investment decision can be efficient without considering a stock's valuation. Whether a stock's current price rightly reflects the intrinsic value of the underlying business and the company's growth prospects is an essential determinant of its future price performance.

Comparing the current value of a company's valuation multiples, such as its price-to-earnings (P/E), price-to-sales (P/S), and price-to-cash flow (P/CF), to its own historical values helps ascertain whether its stock is fairly valued, overvalued, or undervalued, whereas comparing the company relative to its peers on these parameters gives a good sense of how reasonable its stock price is.

As part of the Zacks Style Scores system, the Zacks Value Style Score (which evaluates both traditional and unconventional valuation metrics) organizes stocks into five groups ranging from A to F (A is better than B; B is better than C; and so on), making it helpful in identifying whether a stock is overvalued, rightly valued, or temporarily undervalued.

Silicon Motion is graded D on this front, indicating that it is trading at a premium to its peers. Click here to see the values of some of the valuation metrics that have driven this grade.

Bottom Line

The facts discussed here and much other information on Zacks.com might help determine whether or not it's worthwhile paying attention to the market buzz about Silicon Motion. However, its Zacks Rank #3 does suggest that it may perform in line with the broader market in the near term.

news.Title: 〈台幣〉台積電法說前夕市場觀望 匯市高低洗盤1.5角微升1.2分
news.Content:
觀望美國關鍵消費者物價指數(CPI)報告發布，加上台積電 (2330-TW) (TSM-US) 法說會前夕市場觀望氣氛濃厚，新台幣兌美元匯率今(14)日呈現震盪整理走勢。早盤隨台股開高帶動一度反彈，但隨後外資持續在台股提款並匯出，新台幣升幅逐步收斂，全天高低震盪波動，高低震盪達1.5角，持續在32元整數關卡上演攻防戰，最終以微升1.2分的32.073元兌 1 美元作收。

台北外匯市場新台幣兌美元匯率今日以32.060元開盤，微升2.5分；盤中在台股衝高與出口商拋匯帶動下，最高一度升至32.010元，隨後在外資匯出賣壓湧現下由升轉跌，最低下探至32.160元，高低震盪達1.5角；終場升幅大幅收斂，收在32.073元，微升1.2分，升幅約0.04%。台北外匯市場成交金額為22.24億美元，元太外匯市場成交金額為11.595億美元，兩市合計總成交量達33.835億美元，顯示匯市交投氣氛依然十分熱絡。

從國際匯市來看，美元指數自先前高檔溫和回落，目前在102點附近進行盤整。由於市場正密切關注即將公佈的美國通膨數據，以及美聯儲（Fed）未來降息路徑，國際主要貨幣包含歐元與日元呈現窄幅震盪。歐美主要股市高檔整理，亞洲股市今日則出現洗盤格局，整體國際資金流向仍受到總體經濟數據影響。

國內股市方面，台股今日高低波動劇烈，早盤在台積電及半導體族群衝高帶動下，一度大漲超過700點，一舉衝上49000點大關。然而，高檔獲利了結賣壓傾巢而出，尾盤漲幅明顯收斂，終場上漲284.52點，收在48625.83點，成交量放大至9286.24億元，大盤留長上影線。

籌碼面部分，台北外匯與股票市場連動密切，三大法人今日在台股合計賣超153.97億元。其中，外資持續站在賣方，單日賣超約159億元，已連續六個交易日呈現淨賣超，持續將資金匯出；自營商亦順勢調節；僅有投信獨自力挺台股，逆勢加碼買超161.11億元

news.Title: The S&P 500 Is Dangerously Concentrated in 5 Tech Giants. Are They Still Buys?
news.Content:
The S&P 500 (SNPINDEX: ^GSPC) is no longer as balanced as it has been in the past, with the index's top five positions making up nearly 30% of its holdings. This is the most concentrated the S&P 500 has ever been, and these tech five stocks -- Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA), Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL), Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT), Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOGL) (NASDAQ: GOOG), and Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN) -- will play a crucial role in the benchmark's performance, as well as in the performance of all the exchange-traded funds (ETFs), like the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (NYSEMKT: VOO), that track it.

Let's see if these five tech stocks look like buys.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Nvidia

Nvidia is the main arms dealer in the artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure race, with its graphics processing units (GPUs) as the primary chips powering AI workloads. The company has a huge moat in AI model training, as most early AI code was written on its CUDA software platform for its chips. Meanwhile, over the years, it has evolved into a comprehensive AI infrastructure player that offers end-to-end solutions for specific AI tasks, including training, inference , and agentic AI.

Wherever AI infrastructure spending goes, Nvidia is sure to follow, given its market position. With spending predicted to continue to soar and the stock cheap, with under a 14.5 times forward P/E based on fiscal 2028 (ending January), Nvidia remains a buy.

Apple

Apple has one of the best business models on the planet, as its ecosystem locks in customers and keeps them there. While its hardware, like the iPhone and MacBook, is the draw, it generates a lot of high-margin service revenue from selling cloud storage, commissions on apps and subscriptions, getting a small cut on transactions through Apple Pay, and through its revenue-sharing deal with Alphabet to allow Google to be the default search engine on its devices.

At 35 times forward P/E, the stock is a bit pricey, which could limit upside, but investors are getting a great compounding company that should perform well over the long term.

Microsoft

Microsoft is a leading cloud computing and enterprise productivity software-as-a-service (SaaS) company that also owns 27% of ChatGPT maker OpenAI. Its Azure cloud unit has shown consistent, rapid growth of more than 30% each quarter over the past three years, while it has a huge computing backlog of $678 billion anchored by commitments from OpenAI.

Story Continues

At the same time, given how entrenched its software is in the enterprise space, it's also becoming an AI software winner. It's seeing strong adoption of its AI assistant, Copilot, with paid users nearly doubling sequentially last quarter to 30 million seats. With the company firing on all cylinders, the stock looks reasonably valued, trading at 27 times fiscal 2027 analyst estimates (ending in June 2027) and just above 22.5 times fiscal 2028 consensus estimates.

Alphabet

While best known for Google Search, Alphabet is the most complete AI name, having both its own top-tier AI model and chips. Its chips business is a real differentiator. It allows Alphabet to train and run inference for its AI models more cheaply than competitors do, while its cloud unit achieves a one-year payback on its AI chip and networking investments when it uses its own chips. On top of that, it has started letting partner Broadcom sell directly to Anthropic, which has opened up another high-margin revenue stream for it.

Trading at a forward P/E of 23 times 2027 analyst estimates, the stock looks attractively valued given its growth and position in the market. I'd buy the stock.

Amazon

Amazon is the market share leader in both cloud computing and e-commerce. Its cloud business is accelerating, and the company thinks this could eventually become a $1 trillion revenue business. It's investing aggressively and has a huge backlog, with backing from Anthropic and OpenAI. It also has an emerging chip business.

On the e-commerce side, the company has been seeing strong operating leverage stemming from its investments in robots, automation, and AI. The company does not get nearly the credit it deserves in this area, in my view, while it's also become one of the world's leading digital ad platforms.

At a forward P/E of 25 times based on 2027 estimates, Amazon is trading at a historically attractive valuation, making it a buy.

The S&P 500 and VOO

While the S&P 500 and ETFs like VOO are now highly concentrated, I still see attractive valuations and strong upside potential in four of the index's top five stocks. Apple is the lone exception; I see it as a little pricey, but it is still one of the world's great compounding businesses, and the stock will work over time.

As such, I wouldn't be too worried about the S&P 500's high concentration levels at this point and would continue to be a buyer of VOO, as well.

news.Title: Prediction: Alphabet Stock Is Going to Soar After Oct. 28
news.Content:
The S&P 500 hit a fresh record high last week, and it's trading at an elevated valuation as investors price in some very high forward expectations for artificial intelligence (AI) companies. As a result, strong corporate earnings are the key to keeping this bull market going, and most technology giants will report their latest quarterly results over the next month.

Google parent Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG)(NASDAQ: GOOGL) is scheduled to release its operating results for the third quarter (ended Sept. 30) on Oct. 28. Its stock happens to be reasonably valued heading into the report, and here's why I predict it could soar in the weeks and months that follow.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Wall Street will be focusing on Google Search and Google Cloud

Alphabet is an incredibly diverse tech conglomerate , but Google Search and Google Cloud are currently its most important businesses. Search accounts for more than half of the company's total revenue, whereas Cloud is the fastest-growing segment.

There were some concerns that AI chatbots would disrupt traditional internet search engines like Google Search, but Alphabet introduced a series of AI features to transform the user experience. AI Overviews, for instance, use text and images to provide AI-generated responses to queries, which appear above the traditional search results. Then there is AI Mode, which opens a chatbot-style interface where users can expand on their original queries by asking additional questions.

During Alphabet's last quarterly conference call, CEO Sundar Pichai said AI Mode had surpassed 1 billion monthly users, and that these new features were driving an increase in Google Search usage overall. This means users are seeing more ads, which is why the platform generated a record $63.3 billion in revenue during the second quarter (ended June 30), up 17% year over year. Investors should look for a fresh update on how AI is improving the search business on Oct. 28.

Google Cloud is also coming off a record second quarter with revenues of $24.8 billion, which represented an accelerated growth rate of 84%. The platform provides its enterprise customers with access to computing capacity from state-of-the-art data centers, and a suite of ready-made foundation models, which are the primary ingredients for developing AI software. As of June 30, Google Cloud had a staggering $514 billion order backlog from customers who were waiting for Alphabet to build more AI infrastructure.

Story Continues

The backlog might be a good predictor of future revenue, so it's one of the main numbers Wall Street analysts will be looking at on Oct. 28. If it increased during the third quarter, it will be a sign that demand for AI computing capacity remains very strong.

Alphabet stock looks attractive heading into Oct. 28

Alphabet's second-quarter earnings soared by 294% year over year to $9.11 per share, mostly because of the Space Exploration Technologies (NASDAQ: SPCX) initial public offering (IPO) in June. Alphabet invested $900 million in SpaceX through a private placement in 2015, but accounting rules required the company to recognize the fair market value of its position after the IPO, which was over $90 billion as of June 30. Hence, there was a huge one-off increase to Alphabet's earnings, which had nothing to do with its operating performance.

With that out of the way, Wall Street's average estimate (provided by Yahoo! Finance) suggests Alphabet's earnings likely stabilized at around $3.02 per share in the third quarter, representing a more modest year-over-year growth rate of 5%.

It's disingenuous to value Alphabet based on its trailing-12-month earnings because of the inflated second-quarter result. But looking ahead, Wall Street thinks the company will generate earnings of $14.98 per share during 2027, placing its stock at a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 23.4. That represents a slight premium to the Nasdaq-100 index which has a forward P/E of 22.1, but I think it's justified given the incredible AI-related strength in Google Search and Google Cloud.

Alphabet stock has returned around 45% over the past 12 months, but I think the company's third-quarter report will lay the groundwork for the next leg of upside, as long as its operating results show further momentum in the search and cloud businesses.

news.Title: Intel vs. Marvell Technology: Which Tech Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
news.Content:
The semiconductor landscape is shifting as artificial intelligence demands new hardware. Deciding between a turnaround giant like Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) and a networking specialist like Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL) requires looking at their 2026 trajectories.

Intel is pivoting toward becoming a world-class foundry while maintaining its CPU dominance. Marvell focuses on the plumbing of the data center, providing the high-speed connectivity needed for modern AI clusters. Both companies compete for space in the global infrastructure market, but they offer distinct financial profiles for investors.

The case for Intel

Intel designs and manufactures x86 processors while scaling Intel Foundry to offer advanced packaging and design enablement to the broader industry. The company is leaning into its manufacturing strength through a deepened partnership with Applied Materials (NASDAQ:AMAT) for next-generation equipment. Intel continues to be a central player among semiconductor stocks as it expands its foundry business.

For the fiscal year ended Dec. 27, 2025, revenue was nearly $52.9 billion, essentially flat (down just 0.5%) compared to the prior year. The company reported a net loss of approximately $267 million. While still in the red, this result was a significant improvement over the previous fiscal year, when it recorded a massive net loss of about $18.8 billion.

Intel carries a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.4, which compares its total debt to the value of shareholder equity. As of its December 2025 balance sheet, its current ratio of 2 indicates it has twice as many short-term assets as liabilities. Free cash flow was negative at nearly $4.9 billion, while stock-based compensation represented roughly 25.1% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation.

The case for Marvell Technology

Marvell Technology focuses on data infrastructure, providing networking and storage solutions that power modern cloud and carrier environments. The company has aggressively expanded its AI portfolio through the recent acquisitions of Celestial AI and Polariton Technologies. Like its peers, Marvell faces significant concentration, with its 10 largest customers representing roughly 82% of total revenue and two specific customers each accounting for more than 10% of sales.

In the fiscal year ended Jan. 31, 2026, revenue reached approximately $8.2 billion, a significant 42.1% increase over the prior year. Net income for the period was close to $2.7 billion, yielding a net margin of 32.6%. This margin reflects the percentage of revenue remaining after all expenses are paid, showing a sharp recovery from the net loss reported in its previous annual report.

Story Continues

The balance sheet shows a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.3 as of January 2026. Its current ratio of 2 suggests a healthy cushion to cover short-term obligations. Free cash flow was roughly $1.4 billion. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 33.8% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since this is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

Risk profile comparison

Intel faces significant pressure from customer concentration, with one distributor and one direct customer together accounting for half of its revenue. Rapid advancements in AI could disrupt its business model if the company fails to keep pace with competitors or if customers choose to design chips internally. Furthermore, Intel's reliance on third-party partners in Taiwan for certain manufacturing stages creates geographic risks related to political instability and global supply chain tensions.

Marvell's recent spree of acquisitions, including XConn Technologies, carries the risk of integration challenges and high financial burdens. The company faces intense competition from established giants like Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA), Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD), and Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO), who are all vying for the same data center sockets. Additionally, carrying $4.5 billion in debt may limit its operational flexibility if interest rates remain high or demand for networking chips slows.

Valuation comparison

Comparing these companies on price reveals a significant gap in how the market values their current sales and future earnings estimates.

Metric

Intel

Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

Which stock would I buy in 2026?

Part of the reason Intel reported that gigantic loss in the previous fiscal year is because it's in the midst of a turnaround. It's pivoting toward providing chip manufacturing services for third parties. In other words, the chipmaker is having to shell out quite a lot of money in order to build fabrication plants. That spending will likely continue, as turning around a ship of Intel's size is neither a fast nor an easy endeavor. The U.S. government's investment in Intel also gives me pause.

Marvell concerns me less. It's not in the middle of overhauling its business. The company faces customer concentration, but not on the same level as Intel. Marvell's forward P/E is marginally less expensive. And perhaps most importantly, Marvell is growing, and Intel is not. The former's revenue surged more than 40% in its most recent fiscal year, and it flipped from reporting a loss to a healthy profit. Intel can claim neither.

There are too many uncertainties tied to Intel's business makeover. Marvell looks like the better bet here.

news.Title: Best Semiconductor Stocks to Buy and Hold Through 2030
news.Content:
As artificial intelligence (AI) hyperscalers invest hundreds of billions of dollars in infrastructure, demand for advanced processors, custom silicon, networking equipment, and semiconductor manufacturing capacity is accelerating. The biggest winners will be the companies that control the technologies stitching the AI ecosystem together.

For investors looking toward 2030, Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA), Broadcom (NASDAQ: AVGO), and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE: TSM) stand out as three compelling semiconductor stocks to buy and hold.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Nvidia: The platform powering AI factories

Nvidia is no longer simply a graphics processing unit (GPU) company. Its ecosystem now encompasses GPUs, CPUs, CUDA software, high-speed networking, and sophisticated systems that connect clusters of processors inside AI factories.

The company's financial performance reflects its dominance. In fiscal 2024, Nvidia's data center revenue totaled $47.5 billion. Through the second quarter of fiscal 2027, the company's data center business is operating on a run rate toward $328 billion. This level of growth underscores Nvidia's leadership position as hyperscalers race to build AI infrastructure.

Nvidia's next chapter could be even more interesting. The company's Vera Rubin CPU architecture creates new opportunities beyond traditional GPU design, while its networking portfolio is expanding through products such as NVLink, Spectrum-X Ethernet, and InfiniBand.

Nvidia is smartly forging partnerships across the semiconductor supply chain to broaden its reach. The company has made investments in and is collaborating on products with Nokia , Marvell Technology , Coherent , and Lumentum . These moves demonstrate how the company is expanding into telecommunications, custom silicon connectivity, and optical networking.

Meanwhile, Nvidia's technology stack increasingly supports next-generation use cases across autonomous vehicles, robotics, industrial automation, and even space-based computing ambitions. These markets have the potential to create additional growth opportunities beyond traditional data centers.

Nvidia's greatest competitive advantage isn't manufacturing faster processors. It's controlling the hardware and software layers that competitors struggle to replicate at scale.

Story Continues

Broadcom: Dominating the custom silicon opportunity

While Nvidia dominates the merchant GPU market, Broadcom is helping AI developers design specialized processors around their own AI workloads. These chips are known as application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs) and can offer attractive performance and efficiency for particular use cases.

Broadcom works with Alphabet on Google Cloud's Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), while its relationship with Meta Platforms supports the development of Meta Training and Inference Accelerators (MTIA). Moreover, the company is also working with OpenAI on its inference processor, called Jalapeño.

The financial opportunity behind custom silicon is substantial. Broadcom's leadership is guiding toward $58 billion in AI revenue for fiscal 2026, representing an 186% year-over-year increase. Given the company's secured supply and deployment visibility, AI revenue is expected to surge to $115 billion and $230 billion in fiscal 2027 and 2028, respectively. In other words, Broadcom's AI-driven growth is expected to double for three consecutive years.

Similar to Nvidia, Broadcom also benefits from the networking infrastructure required to connect systems within data centers. Its Ethernet switches, networking silicon, and connectivity technologies offer additional avenues to participate in the upside of AI infrastructure spending. As a result, Broadcom is positioned to benefit whether hyperscalers purchase Nvidia GPUs or embrace custom processors.

Taiwan Semi: The backbone of AI chip manufacturing

The common denominator connecting Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices , Broadcom, and many other semiconductor designers is that they depend on Taiwan Semiconductor to manufacture their most advanced processors. TSMC operates the world's largest semiconductor foundry, helping transform chip designs into physical products. Taiwan Semi controls an estimated 72.5% of the global foundry market, compared with Samsung 's 5.9%. That competitive advantage is difficult to overstate.

Whether a hyperscaler orders Nvidia GPUs, AMD accelerators, or custom silicon developed with Broadcom, Taiwan Semi frequently participates in the manufacturing process. The company also supplies advanced logic chips used alongside memory products from manufacturers such as Micron , enabling it to benefit from the ongoing memory supercycle. Unlike individual chip designers, Taiwan Semi doesn't need to predict which AI architecture ultimately dominates.

TSMC's financial results showcase its AI-driven momentum. During the third quarter, revenue reached approximately $46.7 billion, representing roughly 41% year-over-year growth in U.S. dollars. What's encouraging is that the company's catalysts extend beyond today's AI capex. Demand for advanced 2-nanometer manufacturing, sophisticated chip packaging, and increasingly complex AI processors should support years of expansion into the next decade as new applications move into production.

news.Title: Zacks Investment Ideas feature highlights: Meta Platform, Micron, SK Hynix, SanDisk and and ASML
news.Content:
For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – October 14, 2026 – Today, Zacks Investment Ideas feature highlights Meta Platform META, Micron MU, SK Hynix SKHY, SanDisk SNDK and ASML ASML

Bearing AI Headlines: An Artificial Wave of Panic

Misleading AI Headlines Drag Down Memory Names

Over the past few weeks, three bearish AI headlines have dragged down the industry and sparked fear, uncertainty, and doubt among investors. Although short-term price action has been negative and bears have been in control, the headlines are misleading or downright inaccurate. Below are the three headlines:

1. "OpenAI's Annualized Revenue Nears $50B, Below Earlier $70B Reports": Earlier this month, the Financial Times reported that OpenAI's recent revenue growth was $20 billion below what Wall Street had expected. However, the article's editor failed to account for how OpenAI calculates revenue. In reality, the $70 billion revenue figure was never revised down, it was a completely different number. The $70 billion annualized revenue reported in late September by Axios and Reuters included enterprise sales, which more than doubled since July. Conversely, the FT's $50 billion OpenAI revenue figure did not include the full value of sales through cloud partners. In other words, nothing has changed. The $70 billion gross revenue and $50 billion net revenue remained the same, signaling that OpenAI's business is still growing rapidly.

2. "Meta Muse Growth Plateaus": Recent headlines suggest that Meta Platform's agentic AI platform "Muse" is seeing sluggish growth. However, data show that Muse is growing faster than any AI platform since ChatGPT launched in late 2022.

3. "Why this Little Known Chinese Chipmaker Has Caused a Global Stock Rout": Earlier this week, memory-related stocks like Micron, SK Hynix and SanDisk fell amid reports that China-based ChangXin Memory Technologies has made progress on new architecture that will increase memory density on its AI chips. Memory stocks have soared over the past few years as demand has dramatically overwhelmed supply. While a higher memory supply is bearish for names like Micron, investors have overreacted for a few reasons.

First, CXMT has difficulty accessing chipmaking equipment from companies like ASML due to U.S. export controls. Second, the legacy memory makers still have a wide technological advantage over CXMT. In other words, companies are unlikely to dump SKHY or MU in favor of CXMT technology.

Bottom Line

Short-term headline noise has led to bearish price action among AI leaders. However, misinterpreted revenue metrics, overstated platform slowdowns, and exaggerated competitive threats have created an artificial wave of panic.

news.Title: Dear Intel Fans, Mark Your Calendars for October 29
news.Content:
Intel (INTC) will release its third-quarter financial results after the market closes on Thursday, Oct. 29. Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven demand and improving pricing give reason to be optimistic about Intel's Q3, especially as its Data Center and AI (DCAI) business continues to grow rapidly.

Notably, Intel shares have climbed 174.5% so far in 2026 as its operational turnaround is gaining momentum. Strong demand and pricing power have boosted Intel's financials and investors' confidence. However, INTC stock has retreated about 28.8% from its recent high, presenting an attractive entry point, especially as the upcoming results could act as a catalyst.

Dear Nvidia Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for October 13
